PF-05.new_issue_title: 🧾 [Pricing] Admin screens for per-organisation exceptions, individual plans, the audit log and the engine status panel
PF-05.new_issue_body:
## What and why

Owner decision 5 (#243) asks for per-organisation exceptions and a log of every change; decision 6 asks for the environment-aware engine switch. Decision 26 adds personal plans: an individual can have a paid plan in their own name without joining an organisation, through an invisible personal account holder (PF-13).

This adds the screens: an exceptions page per organisation (grant, deny, set or adjust one feature, with an optional end date and a required note), an 'Individual plans' page where a GlobalAdmin finds a person by email and sets their personal plan, a readable audit log, and an engine panel that shows which environment this request is in and whether the engine is on here.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `/platform/exceptions?org=<handle>` lists, creates and switches off overrides, for organisations and personal holders; never deletes.
- [ ] `/platform/individuals`: find a person, see their personal plan (or Free), set it; every change audited.
- [ ] `/platform/audit` lists changes with before/after shown as tables, paginated.
- [ ] Engine panel on `/platform` with audited edits of `billing.pricing_engine_enabled` and `billing.active_environments`.
- [ ] GlobalAdmin guard, CSRF, `__()` strings (seed 033), accessible markup; tests.

## Dependencies

PF-04, PF-01, PF-13.

PF-06.title: Prices and coupons admin on the existing price-book tables, with fixed USD and EUR prices and a currency coverage view
PF-06.plan:
GOAL: GlobalAdmin screens to create and edit rows in tblPricePlans and tblCoupons (schema 036) with audit, and keep tblSubscriptionTiers.tierPriceMonthly / tierPriceAnnual in step. Decision 40 (#243 second set): GBP is the base; the owner sets fixed, rounded prices in USD and EUR here by hand, and the pricing page (PF-07) shows them to visitors in those currencies. Prices are never calculated from GBP by the code. No purchase, redemption or provider integration (that is #58 / #59).

STEP 1 — web/_functions/price_admin.php (functions only, new-style guard; uses g2ml_tierAdminWriteAudit and g2ml_tierAdminIsGlobalAdmin from tier_admin.php, required at call time with function_exists checks). g2ml_priceAdminListPlans(): array|false (JOIN tier name; ordered tierID, currency, billingInterval, sortOrder); g2ml_priceAdminGetPlan(int); g2ml_priceAdminSavePlan(?int $planUID, array $input, int $actorUID): array{success, error, errorCode} validating: planSlug ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,99}$ unique; planName <= 150; tierID must be an existing tier (planType credit_pack/addon/one_off are refused with errorCode 'type_not_supported' in this version); planType in recurring | lifetime | payg_capped; billingInterval month | year required for recurring, NULL otherwise; amount validated with ^\d{1,8}(\.\d{1,2})?$ before binding as a string (never a float); currency in ['GBP','EUR','USD'] (a constant; billing.default_currency must be one of them); trialDays 0-365; for payg_capped: meteredFeatureUID must be an active isMeterable feature, unitPrice ^\d{1,6}(\.\d{1,6})?$, unitSize >= 1, includedUnits >= 0 or empty, capAmount or equivalentPlanUID (an existing active recurring plan of the same tier and currency) — at least one, capBehaviour required; validFrom / validUntil Y-m-d optional and ordered; isDefault, isVisible, isActive (default 0), sortOrder. When isDefault = 1 is saved for (tierID, currency, billingInterval), clear isDefault on the other plans of that group in the same transaction. Dual write (platform design section 3): after saving a recurring plan with isActive = 1 and isDefault = 1 whose currency equals tblSubscriptionTiers.tierCurrency: month → tierPriceMonthly = amount, year → tierPriceAnnual = amount; audit price_plan.create / update with before/after. PURE g2ml_priceAdminCoverage(array $activeTiers, array $plans): array — per tier, per currency (GBP, USD, EUR), per interval (month, year): the amount of the active, visible, default recurring plan, or null for 'not set'. g2ml_priceAdminListCoupons(); g2ml_priceAdminSaveCoupon(?int $couponUID, array $input, int $actorUID): couponCode NULL or ^[A-Z0-9-]{3,50}$ (uppercase the input) unique; couponName <= 255; discountKind in the ENUM; discountValue rules: percentage 0-100, fixed_amount / override_price >= 0 with the money pattern, free_periods → durationPeriods >= 1 required; durationType in the ENUM with durationPeriods / durationUntil required accordingly; applicablePlanUID / applicableTierID / applicablePlanType optional and must exist; minAmount, maxUses, perOrgMaxUses >= 0 or empty; isStackable + stackingGroup <= 50; validFrom / validUntil ordered; isActive default 0; audit coupon.create / update. Never delete plans or coupons (isActive 0 retires them). Every function guarded, prepared statements, transactions, plain-English errors with errorCodes.

STEP 2 — pages/platform/prices/index.php and pages/platform/coupons/index.php (PF-04 conventions): list tables plus one create/edit form (GET ?edit=<id>), CSRF 'platform_plan_save_<id or new>' / 'platform_coupon_save_<id or new>'; money inputs are type='text' inputmode='decimal' with pattern hints (never type=number for money). At the top of the prices page, a 'Currency coverage' table built from g2ml_priceAdminCoverage(): rows = active tiers, columns = GBP / USD / EUR × monthly / annual, each cell the formatted amount or a visible 'not set' (with visually hidden text for screen readers), and a plain note: 'Set fixed, rounded USD and EUR prices here (decision 40). The pricing page shows them to visitors in those currencies. Where one is not set, visitors see the GBP price with an approximate figure, labelled as charged in GBP. Prices are never converted automatically.' Other plain notes: 'A plan is not offered until it is active and visible', 'Coupons cannot be redeemed until online billing exists (#58); this is groundwork.' Link both pages from /platform.

STEP 3 — strings: seed web/_sql/seeds/034_price_admin_translations.sql (INSERT IGNORE, 'Admin — Plans and pricing'): priceadmin.* keys for every label, the plan-type and cap-behaviour explanations, the discount kinds, priceadmin.coverage_heading 'Currency coverage', priceadmin.coverage_not_set 'not set', priceadmin.coverage_note (the text above).

STEP 4 — tests: tests/unit/price_admin_test.php: the money pattern, coupon-code normalisation, per-type required-field rules (PURE validators g2ml_priceAdminValidatePlanInput(array): array{errors} and g2ml_priceAdminValidateCouponInput(array)), and Coverage (a tier with GBP month only → USD and EUR null; an inactive or non-default plan is ignored). tests/integration/price_admin_test.php: save a monthly GBP default recurring plan for 'basic' at 5.49 → tierPriceMonthly 5.49; a USD default plan for 'basic' at 6.99 leaves tierPriceMonthly unchanged (not the tier's currency) and shows in the coverage; a second default for the same group clears the first's isDefault; a payg_capped plan without a cap or equivalent → refused; a coupon with code 'launch-25' stored as 'LAUNCH-25'; audit rows written; clean up.

STEP 5 — docs (last): docs/DATABASE.md price book paragraph (what the admin writes; fixed USD/EUR prices; what remains unbuilt); handoff.

VERIFY: php -l; php tests/run.php, exit code read directly; integration with a database.
acceptance_criteria: Plans (recurring monthly/annual, lifetime, PAYG-capped) in GBP, USD and EUR and coupons can be created and edited by a GlobalAdmin, never deleted; new rows start inactive
Saving an active default recurring plan in the tier's currency updates tierPriceMonthly/tierPriceAnnual in the same transaction; one default per (tier, currency, interval)
A currency coverage table shows, per tier, which fixed GBP / USD / EUR prices are set and which are missing; prices are never converted by the code
All input validated by pure functions with unit tests; money handled as validated strings, never floats; every change audited; strings seeded in seed 034; suites green
PF-06.new_issue_title: 💷 [Pricing] Admin screens for prices (GBP, USD and EUR; monthly, annual, PAYG caps) and coupons on the existing price-book tables
PF-06.new_issue_body:
## What and why

Owner decision 5 (#243): prices and coupons are managed from the admin now, as groundwork for billing. The tables already exist (tblPricePlans, tblCoupons in schema 036) but nothing writes them. Decision 40: GBP is the base, and the owner sets fixed, rounded prices in USD and EUR here by hand; the code never converts prices.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `/platform/prices`: recurring (monthly / annual), lifetime and PAYG-capped plans per tier in GBP, USD or EUR; new plans start inactive; one default plan per tier, currency and interval.
- [ ] A 'currency coverage' table shows which fixed prices are set and which are missing for each tier.
- [ ] Saving an active default plan in the tier's own currency updates the tier's price columns in the same transaction.
- [ ] `/platform/coupons`: percentage, fixed amount, free periods and price-override coupons; codes stored upper-case; new coupons start inactive.
- [ ] Nothing is deleted; every change is audited; pure validators with unit tests; strings seeded (seed 034).

## What this does not do

No purchases, no redemption, no payment provider. Those stay in #58 and #59.

## Dependencies

PF-04, PF-05 (same overview page).

PF-07.title: Public pricing page generated from the tier, price and feature data, in the visitor's currency (guessed from location, with a switcher) and with approximate figures for other currencies
PF-07.plan:
GOAL: web/Go2My.Link/public_html/pages/pricing/index.php shows exactly what the database says (platform design section 7), in the visitor's currency, as DECIDED in decision 40 (#243 second set): GBP is the base; the owner sets fixed, rounded prices in USD and EUR in the price admin (PF-06); the page shows the visitor's currency, guessed from their location, with a switcher; for any other currency it shows the GBP price plus an 'approximately' figure labelled as charged in GBP, from the daily exchange rate stored by PF-14. The approximate figure is information only: the charged price never changes, and real prices are NEVER converted automatically. Nothing about tiers or features is hard-coded afterwards. STEP 1 — web/_functions/pricing.php additions (after g2ml_pricingGetLimit()): - g2ml_pricingResolveTierFeatures(string $tierID): array|false — _g2ml_pricingFetchFeatures() + _g2ml_pricingFetchTierFeatures($tierID) reduced with _g2ml_pricingReduceLatestEffective(); merge per feature with _g2ml_pricingResolveFeatureValue($featureRow, $tierRow, []) (no org overrides); return ['' => ['value' => ..., 'isUnlimited' => ..., 'valueType' => ...]]; request-cached in $GLOBALS['g2ml_pricing_tier_features_cache'][$tierID] (cleared by g2ml_clearPricingCache()); false on any failure; never throws. Docblock: ignores the master switch on purpose. - g2ml_pricingListPricingPageFeatures(): array|false — features with isActive = 1 AND showOnPricingPage = 1, ordered by category then sortOrder. - PURE g2ml_pricingFormatMoney(string $amount, string $currency): string — '0.00' or '0' → '' (the caller prints __('pricing.free_price')); GBP '£', EUR '€', USD '$' as a prefix; every other code → $currency . ' ' . number; decimals 2, except the zero-decimal currencies JPY, KRW, ISK, HUF and IDR (a constant list) → 0; number_format with '.' and ','. Never NumberFormatter (intl may be absent). - g2ml_pricingListPublicPlans(string $currency): array|false — SELECT planUID, tierID, billingInterval, amount, currency, isDefault, sortOrder FROM tblPricePlans WHERE isActive = 1 AND isVisible = 1 AND planType = 'recurring' AND currency = ? AND region IS NULL AND (validFrom IS NULL OR validFrom <= NOW()) AND (validUntil IS NULL OR validUntil > NOW()) ORDER BY tierID, billingInterval, isDefault DESC, sortOrder ASC; PURE g2ml_pricingPickPlanPerInterval(array $rows): array keyed [tierID][interval] → first row. - PURE g2ml_pricingCurrencyForCountry(?string $countryCode): string — GB, GG, JE, IM → 'GBP'; US, PR, GU, VI, AS, MP → 'USD'; the euro area and euro users (AT, BE, HR, CY, EE, FI, FR, DE, GR, IE, IT, LV, LT, LU, MT, NL, PT, SK, SI, ES, AD, MC, SM, VA, ME, XK) → 'EUR'; then a fixed map to the other currencies the rate source publishes: AU AUD, CA CAD, CH CHF, LI CHF, JP JPY, NZ NZD, SE SEK, NO NOK, DK DKK, PL PLN, CZ CZK, HU HUF, RO RON, BG BGN, IS ISK, TR TRY, IN INR, SG SGD, HK HKD, CN CNY, KR KRW, BR BRL, MX MXN, ZA ZAR, IL ILS, MY MYR, TH THB, ID IDR, PH PHP; anything else or null → 'GBP'. Uppercase the input first. - PURE g2ml_pricingCountryFromAcceptLanguage(?string $header): ?string — take the first language tag; return its region subtag when it is exactly two letters (en-US → 'US', pt-BR → 'BR'); 'fr', 'es-419', empty or malformed → null. - g2ml_pricingGuessVisitorCountry(): ?string — when function_exists('g2ml_shouldTrack') and g2ml_shouldTrack() is true AND g2ml_geolocationAvailable() → g2ml_geolocateIP(g2ml_getClientIP())['countryCode'] ?? null (used in memory only for this response; never stored or logged; comment it); otherwise, or when that gives nothing, g2ml_pricingCountryFromAcceptLanguage($_SERVER['HTTP_ACCEPT_LANGUAGE'] ?? null). A Do-Not-Track visitor's IP is not looked up (in the spirit of decision 30). - PURE g2ml_pricingDisplayCurrencies(array $fxAvailable): array — ['GBP','USD','EUR'] followed by every currency code with a fresh rate (from PF-14's g2ml_fxGetRate), sorted, unique. - PURE g2ml_pricingPageBuildModel(array $tiers, array $features, array $valuesByTier, array $plansByCurrency, string $displayCurrency, ?array $fx): array — tiers (name, description) and, per tier and interval (month, year), a price block: (1) the tier's price is 0 in GBP → 'Free' in every currency; (2) $displayCurrency is GBP → the GBP plan (falling back to tierPriceMonthly / tierPriceAnnual when no plan exists); (3) $displayCurrency is USD or EUR AND a plan exists in that currency for that tier and interval → that fixed price, no approximation; (4) otherwise → the GBP price as the real price, plus approx = round(GBP amount × fx['rate']) formatted in the display currency (2 decimals, or 0 for zero-decimal currencies) ONLY when $fx is not null; when $fx is null only the GBP price is shown. Each block carries a flag chargedInGBP (true in case 4). Categories → rows → cells per tier exactly as the first plan ('yes'|'no'|'number'|'unlimited'|'quota'). STEP 2 — the page. Resolve the display currency: $requested = strtoupper((string) ($_GET['currency'] ?? '')); if it matches ^[A-Z]{3}$ and is in g2ml_pricingDisplayCurrencies() → use it; else g2ml_pricingCurrencyForCountry(g2ml_pricingGuessVisitorCountry()), and if that currency is neither GBP/USD/EUR nor has a fresh rate → 'GBP'. The choice is not stored anywhere (no cookie, nothing to consent to); the switcher is a GET form:
with a labelled
acceptance_criteria: The pricing page lists active tiers, prices and a feature matrix from the database; no tier or feature text is hard-coded

The display currency is guessed from the visitor's location (IP only when they do not send Do Not Track and geolocation is on, else the browser language), can be changed with a no-JavaScript switcher, and is not stored

GBP, and USD / EUR where the owner has set a fixed price, are shown as real prices; any other case shows the GBP price with an 'approximately' figure labelled as charged in GBP, only when a fresh daily rate exists; real prices are never converted

PF-09.new_issue_title: 📈 [Analytics] Keep click counts for ever: daily aggregate table written on the redirect, history backfill, and a purge guard
PF-09.new_issue_body:
## What and why

Owner decision 7 (#243): counts are kept for ever; IP addresses are removed after 90 days (configurable); the location worked out at click time is kept. Today every click is one row in the activity log with the visitor's IP. The retention job can blank the IP and, if the purge is ever switched on, delete the rows, and then the counts are gone too.

This adds a small table of daily counts (per link per day, split by country, device type, referring website, browser and operating system) that holds no personal data and is never purged. The redirect writes it directly in one statement, so it does not depend on the scheduled-jobs endpoint. A backfill job fills in history from the existing log, and the purge sweep is stopped from deleting any day whose counts do not exist yet.

**Do Not Track (decision 30):** a visitor who sends Do Not Track adds 1 to the day's total only. Nothing else about them is stored, and their IP address is not looked up.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] New table `tblAnalyticsDaily` (schema 039, migration 031): counts only, no IPs, no user agents, referrer reduced to its website name.
- [ ] Every successful redirect adds one to the day's rows; a failure is logged and never stops the redirect.
- [ ] Do-Not-Track visitors count in the total only, with no IP lookup (tested).
- [ ] Bots are counted separately.
- [ ] Backfill job `aggregate`, safe to re-run, stopping at the day live counting began.
- [ ] The purge sweep refuses to delete a day that has not been counted; the anonymise sweep also trims referrers to their website name.
- [ ] Settings documented; unit and integration tests.

## Dependencies

The direct-access guard fix (#198). The backfill needs the #178 trigger to run through the endpoint. Relates to #167, #178, #43.

PF-12.new_issue_title: ⚖️ [Compliance] Switch the retention clean-up on for launch and fill the privacy policy's retention sentences from the same settings
PF-12.new_issue_body:
## What and why

Owner decisions 7, 8 and 31 (#243). IP addresses are removed after a configurable number of days (90), the location worked out at click time is kept, and rows are kept without identifiers (no purge). Decision 31: the automatic clean-up is ON at launch. Today it ships switched off, and the privacy policy hard-codes '90 days' and promises things the code does not do (#167).

This does two things.

1. **Clean-up on.** Fresh installs get the clean-up switched on by default. Existing databases get a migration (048) that switches it on. Because every site and environment shares one database, that migration is a deliberate launch step on the pre-launch checklist: once it runs, IP addresses older than 90 days are removed and cannot be brought back.
2. **Policy wording from the settings.** The privacy policy reads the same settings as the clean-up job and prints them, with honest wording if the job is ever switched off. It also gains a row for the daily statistics counts, which hold no personal data and are kept indefinitely.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Seed 020 seeds the clean-up ON (90 days, purge 0); migration 048 switches existing databases on and is safe to run twice.
- [ ] Pure helpers pick the numbers and the wording variant from the settings (unit tests for every branch).
- [ ] Section 7 rows and the IP line in 2.2 use new keys with `{ip_days}`, `{purge_days}`, `{grace_days}`, `{export_hours}` placeholders (seed 039).

The scheduled-jobs fix (#198). Relates to #167, #178.

LP-27.new_issue_title: 🧱 [LinksPage] Plan foundation: individuals count as Free (or their personal plan), a strict limit check for paid extras, per-organisation counting, and a visitor attempt limiter
LP-27.new_issue_body:
## What and why

Every LinksPage feature planned under #243 asks the same questions: "is this on the page owner's plan?" and "how many does their organisation already have?". Three things must be solved once, before those features are built.

1. **Individuals must count as Free (owner decisions 25 and 26).** People without an organisation sit in the shared `[default]` organisation, which the plan checks never limit. This adds one helper that treats an individual's page as Free, or as their own personal plan when they have bought one (the invisible personal account holder, PF-13). GlobalAdmins stay unlimited.
2. **The existing number check says "allowed" when something breaks.** That is right for creating links, but wrong for paid extras such as password pages, uploads and email capture. This adds a strict version that says "no" on a failure.
3. **Visitor forms need a rate limit that Do Not Track cannot bypass.** The activity log skips Do-Not-Track visitors, so it cannot count attempts. A small table stores a scrambled form of the visitor's IP address (never the address itself) for 24 hours.

It also adds one function where every render-time plan check lives, so the public page and the owner's preview always follow the same rules, and it routes the existing custom-HTML check through the same helper.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `g2ml_featureLimitStrict()` denies on a system error, an unknown feature or a wrong type; otherwise it matches `g2ml_featureLimit()` exactly.
- [ ] `web/_functions/linkspage_plan.php`: the plan helper (individuals → personal plan or Free; GlobalAdmins unlimited), allowed/quota wrappers, per-organisation counting on the stored handle.
- [ ] `tblLinksPageAttempts` (schema 040, migration 032) with limiter functions that fail closed.
- [ ] `g2ml_linkspageDecorateModel()` called from the public and preview model builders.
- [ ] Unit and integration tests; docs.

## Security and privacy

No raw IP addresses stored. Paid extras fail closed.

## Dependencies

The personal account holder (PF-13). Every later LinksPage item uses this. Relates to #215, #216, #243.

LP-24.title: Apply colours consistently in every template and choose readable text colours automatically
LP-24.plan:
GOAL: every template uses {{background}} for the page background and {{theme}} for the accent, text on each is automatically black or white for WCAG 2.1 AA, and the editor warns when a chosen pair is hard to read.

STEP 1 renderer: PURE g2ml_linkspageRelativeLuminance(string $hex): float (WCAG 2.1 formula, #RGB expanded), g2ml_linkspageContrastRatio(string $hexA, string $hexB): float, g2ml_linkspageReadableTextColour(string $hexBackground): string ('#000000' or '#FFFFFF', whichever gives the higher ratio). g2ml_linkspageValidateHexColour() accepts only #RGB or #RRGGBB (check; tighten if it accepts more) and returns uppercase #RRGGBB. g2ml_renderLinksPage() adds data 'on_theme' and 'on_background'; ApplyTemplate substitutes {{on_theme}} and {{on_background}}. Header: 12 placeholders.

STEP 2 templates: rewrite each system template's CSS so that the container background is {{background}}, body text colour is {{on_background}}, link buttons use background {{theme}} and colour {{on_theme}} (or, for outline styles, border {{theme}} and colour {{on_background}}), secondary text uses opacity rather than fixed greys, hover/focus styles keep the ratio, and a prefers-reduced-motion block disables transitions. Keep LP-08's rules. Edit seed 004 (full CSS per template) and new migration web/_sql/migrations/033_linkspage_template_colours.sql: per slug UPDATE tblLinksPageTemplates SET templateCSS = '<final CSS>' WHERE templateSlug = ? AND isSystem = 1 AND templateCSS NOT LIKE '%{{on_theme}}%' (system templates are not user-editable, so replacing their CSS is safe; say so in the header). modern's inline style attribute keeps its gradient but its text colour becomes {{on_background}}.

STEP 3 manage: after validating both colours, compute the text-on-accent ratio (readable text vs theme) — always >= 4.5 by construction — and the raw theme-vs-background ratio; when the accent-against-background ratio is below 3:1 (WCAG 1.4.11 for button boundaries) return a non-blocking warning: add 'warnings' => ['low_contrast'] to the Create/Update success result (new key; callers that ignore it are unaffected).

STEP 4 admin: create/edit show an alert-warning role="status" with __('linkspage.contrast_warning', ['ratio' => formatted to one decimal]) after a save that returned the warning; below the colour inputs a short help line __('linkspage.contrast_help').

STEP 5 seed web/_sql/seeds/042_linkspage_contrast_translations.sql: linkspage.contrast_warning 'Your accent colour is hard to see against your background (contrast {ratio}:1). Your page still works, but some visitors may struggle to see the link buttons. Try a darker or lighter accent.'; linkspage.contrast_help 'Text on your buttons is set to black or white automatically so it is always readable.'

STEP 6 tests: tests/unit/linkspage_contrast_test.php: luminance of #FFFFFF = 1 and #000000 = 0; ratio(#FFF, #000) = 21; #767676 on #FFFFFF about 4.54; readable text for #1E88E5 and #FFEB3B; invalid hex rejected; every placeholder substituted in a render of each seeded template (read seed 004 with a regex like the existing render test does, or use a fixture). Integration: saving a pale accent on white returns the low_contrast warning.

VERIFY: php -l; unit exit code; import migration 033 twice.
acceptance_criteria: Every system template uses {{background}}, {{theme}}, {{on_background}} and {{on_theme}}; migration 033 is re-runnable
Text on buttons and page is automatically black or white; contrast helpers unit-tested against WCAG reference values
Low accent/background contrast gives a non-blocking warning with translated text (seed 042)
Hex validation accepts only #RGB and #RRGGBB

It is built straight after LP-08 because both rewrite the template styles, and before the seven new templates (#238) so they follow the same colour rules from the start. AND userUID = ?; logActivity('linkspage_password_set') with no password in the data. g2ml_linkspageManageClearPassword(): always allowed; hash NULL, version + 1. GetPageForOwner selects both columns but callers never echo the hash.

STEP 4 unlock token (new functions in web/Lnks.page/_functions/linkspage_public.php or a new linkspage_unlock.php required by it): PURE g2ml_linkspageUnlockSign(int $pageUID, int $version, int $expiresAt, string $key): string = hash_hmac('sha256', 'lp-unlock|v1|' . pageUID . '|' . version . '|' . expiresAt, $key); build token 'v1.<pageUID>.<version>.<expiresAt>.<sig>'; verify (hash_equals, version match, not expired, pageUID match); key ENCRYPTION_KEY_SECONDARY (the 'lp-unlock' prefix keeps it separate from the age-gate token). Cookie name 'g2ml_lpu_' . pageUID, host-only, Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite Lax, path '/'.

STEP 5 pipeline slot 2 (BEFORE the age gate and before any click redirect): the resolver public SELECTs add accessPasswordHash, accessPasswordVersion; DecorateModel block 'Password (LP-13, #228)' sets page['isPasswordProtected'] = hash not NULL (whatever the plan: a stored password always locks — fail safe after a downgrade), and REMOVES accessPasswordHash from the model for context 'preview' after noting the flag (never passed to the renderer in either context: the pipeline reads the hash via a separate prepared SELECT accessPasswordHash, accessPasswordVersion FROM tblLinksPages WHERE pageUID = ? just before verifying, so the hash is not carried in the model at all — do that, and drop it from the public SELECT again; comment why). STEP 7 tests: tests/unit/linkspage_unlock_token_test.php (valid, tampered signature, wrong page, old version, expired, malformed). tests/integration/linkspage_password_test.php: Free cannot set (feature_unavailable); Premium sets 3 and the 4th page is refused; changing an existing password is allowed at the limit; protected page GET shows the lock screen without the title or any item URL; wrong password records an attempt; the 11th try in the window is refused even with the right password; right password sets a cookie and the page renders; a password change invalidates the old cookie; a downgraded org's protected page stays locked; the click route on a protected page without the cookie shows the lock screen; the custom-domain fallback shows the lock screen.

STEP 8 docs: docs/DATABASE.md columns; security notes in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md; handoff.

acceptance_criteria: Password stored only as password_hash(); never echoed, logged or carried in the page model

LP-13.issue_comment: Planned on 2026-09-21 under #243 decision 4 (LP-13). Password-protected pages become a NUMBER per organisation (proposed Premium 3, Enterprise unlimited, none on Free and Basic). LP-28.new_issue_title: 🔒 [LinksPage] Narrow page images to our own server now that uploads exist
LP-28.new_issue_body:
## What and why

Owner decision 11 (#243): images from other websites were allowed on public pages for now (#221), and the rule is narrowed to our own server once image upload exists (#231). This does that. Loading images only from our own server means a visitor's browser no longer contacts third-party sites just by opening a page. It also closes a route for tracking pixels disguised as avatars.

Decision 29 means every plan, Free included, can upload one avatar per page, so no page is left unable to show an avatar.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The page security policy allows images only from our own address and built-in data images.
- [ ] Avatars and link icons that point at another website are no longer shown (the default image appears instead), and new ones cannot be saved. Old values are kept, not deleted.
- [ ] The editor explains why an image disappeared and offers the upload.
- [ ] Tests updated; strings seeded (seed 045).

## Dependencies

#231 (image upload).

LP-29.new_issue_title: 🎨 [LinksPage] Customise or upload your own template (cleaned like custom HTML, shipped switched off)
LP-29.new_issue_body:
## What and why

Owner decision 13 (#243): templates that owners customise or upload are available on paid plans through the plan admin (`linkspage.template_upload`). Uploaded templates go through the same cleaner and script block as custom HTML, and ship switched off until a security review.

An owner can copy a built-in template and edit its HTML and CSS, or upload a template file. The placeholders ({{name}}, {{links}} and so on) are kept. Anything that could run code is removed on save and again when the page is shown, and the page is served under the policy that blocks all scripts.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Operator switch `linkspage.user_templates_enabled`, seeded OFF.
- [ ] Copy-and-edit and upload, limited to plans with `linkspage.template_upload`.
- [ ] Cleaned on save and on render; placeholders only in text and the avatar image; colours through CSS variables the page defines itself.
- [ ] Pages using them get the no-script security policy; denied or deleted templates fall back to Default.
- [ ] Tests; PRE_LAUNCH_CHECKLIST.md records the review.

## Dependencies

The seven new templates issue (#238), the plan registry update, and the shared visitor routine (#229). Must not be switched on before #207 (CSS escape decoding) lands.

LP-32.new_issue_title: ✅ [LinksPage] Admin-awarded Verified badge on request, with a written verification policy
LP-32.new_issue_body:
## What and why

Owner decision 10 (#243): besides the automatic website check (#233), there is an admin-awarded "Verified" badge, granted on request under a written verification policy (`docs/VERIFICATION_POLICY.md`). Plans control who may request verification, never who gets it: a badge can never simply be bought.

Decision 37 settles three rules:

1. The request form stays switched off until the owner approves the policy.
2. Once granted, the badge survives a downgrade.
3. The badge is removed automatically if the page's name or address changes, so a verified page cannot be renamed into someone else.

## What this adds

- A request form for owners on plans that include `linkspage.verified_badge`.
- A GlobalAdmin review screen to approve, reject or remove, with a note to the owner and a log entry.
- A badge that looks different from the website label.
- A draft `docs/VERIFICATION_POLICY.md`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] New table for requests (schema 042, migration 040) and badge columns on the page.
- [ ] Server-side GlobalAdmin check on every decision.
- [ ] The three rules above, each tested.
- [ ] Requests included in the data export; deleted with the page.

## Dependencies

The website check issue (#233) and the plan admin screens (for the admin menu).

STEP 2 — web/_functions/linkspage_leads.php additions (all ownership-scoped by joining tblLinksPages p ON p.pageUID = l.pageUID WHERE p.userUID = ?): g2ml_linkspageLeadsList(int $userUID, int $pageUID, int $limit, int $offset): rows with the decrypted email (g2ml_decrypt; a failed decrypt shows '(unreadable)' and logs); g2ml_linkspageLeadsDelete(int $userUID, int $leadUID); g2ml_linkspageLeadsDeleteAllForPage(int $userUID, int $pageUID); g2ml_linkspageLeadsExportCSV(int $userUID, int $pageUID): streams 'email,confirmed_at_utc,consent_version' for confirmed rows only; PURE g2ml_linkspageCsvSafeCell(string $value): string (prefix a single quote when the value starts with = + - @ tab or carriage return; formula-injection guard, commented); logActivity('linkspage_leads_export') with the row count only. LP-31.new_issue_title: 📮 [LinksPage] Email capture for creators: sign-up list, CSV export, deletion, automatic clean-up, and data export and erasure
LP-31.new_issue_body:
## What and why

Owner decision 9 (#243) asks for email capture to include a CSV export, automatic deletion, and coverage in data export and deletion. The visitor side is #234. This is the creator's side.

Decision 35 sets three data rules, all built here:

1. A creator's data export includes the sign-up list they collected.
2. Anyone's data export lists the sign-ups made with their own email address (which page, and when).
3. Erasing an account deletes both the creator's lists and that person's own sign-ups everywhere.

## What this adds

- A sign-up list per page, visible only to the page owner, with delete and delete-all.
- A CSV download of confirmed addresses, protected against spreadsheet formula injection.
- Automatic clean-up in the retention job: unconfirmed sign-ups after 7 days, confirmed ones after a configurable number of months (24 proposed, for the legal review).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Ownership checked in SQL on every read, download and delete.
- [ ] Clean-up runs with the retention job.
- [ ] Each of the three data rules has its own integration test.
- [ ] Strings and settings seeded (seed 052).

## Dependencies

#234 (visitor side). Builds on #219 (LinksPages in data export and deletion).

LP-26.title: Public LinksPages: 60-second browser caching for plain views, and no session unless the page needs one
LP-26.plan:
GOAL: #241, as DECIDED in decision 41 (#243 second set): a plain public view creates no session file and may be cached by the visitor's browser for 60 seconds (setting linkspage.public_cache_seconds, 0 turns it off). Pages with an age gate, a password or a form are never cached. SX-213's rule stays in force: any request with a signed-in user gets 'no-store, private' (fixes design note 8).

STEP 1 — session start refactor: web/_functions/session.php add g2ml_sessionStartConfigured(): bool containing exactly today's page_init.php Step 7 body (name, ini settings, cookie params from g2ml_sessionCookieDomain, session_start, periodic regeneration). page_init.php Step 7 calls it, EXCEPT when defined('G2ML_SESSION_MODE') && G2ML_SESSION_MODE === 'lazy' AND the request method is GET or HEAD AND no G2ML session cookie is present — then it defines G2ML_SESSION_DEFERRED = true and skips. Add g2ml_sessionEnsureStarted(): bool (no-op when active; otherwise g2ml_sessionStartConfigured()). Behaviour for every other component and for POSTs is unchanged; say so in both docblocks. Keep SX-213's private-cache block working: it must see a session when one exists (when the session is deferred there is by definition no signed-in user, so its helper returns no headers for the public component). Check every function used on the lnks.page path that touches $_SESSION (g2ml_generateCSRFToken, i18n locale detection, cookie consent) and make sure each either tolerates no session or is only reached after g2ml_sessionEnsureStarted(); list what was checked in the commit.

STEP 2 — lnks.page index.php: define('G2ML_SESSION_MODE', 'lazy') before requiring page_init.php (with a comment). The media route (LP-16) needs no session.

STEP 3 — pipeline (linkspage_public.php slot 7, and wherever a form is rendered): call g2ml_sessionEnsureStarted() before rendering anything that carries a CSRF field (age-gate interstitial, unlock screen, sign-up form, lead confirm pages) and before handling any POST. The cache decision is PURE g2ml_linkspagePublicCachePolicy(array $facts): string with facts method, sessionActive, isGated, isProtected, hasForm, embedExpanded, isRedirect, cacheSeconds → 'public, max-age=<n>' only when the method is GET, no session is active, not gated, not protected, no form, no expanded embed, not a redirect, and n > 0; otherwise 'private, no-store'. Clamp cacheSeconds to 0-3600 before use. Send it as Cache-Control; for the public case remove any Pragma header and make sure no Set-Cookie header is being sent in that response (headers_list() check; if one is present, fall back to 'private, no-store' and log once — a cached response must never carry a cookie). The custom-domain surface uses the same policy.

STEP 4 — seed web/_sql/seeds/054_linkspage_cache_setting.sql: linkspage.public_cache_seconds ('60', integer, 'How long a visitor''s browser may reuse a plain LinksPage view (decision 41). Edits and unpublishing can take this long to show. Pages with an age gate, a password or a form are never cached. 0 turns caching off.').

STEP 5 — tests: unit tests/unit/linkspage_cache_policy_test.php for every branch of the policy, including sessionActive true → no-store, cacheSeconds 0 → no-store, cacheSeconds 99999 clamped to 3600, and a Set-Cookie fallback helper. Integration: a plain GET on lnks.page (simulate by including the pipeline with G2ML_SESSION_DEFERRED set) sends 'public, max-age=60' and starts no session; an age-gated page starts a session and sends no-store; a page with an active sign-up form sends no-store; a password-protected page sends no-store. tests/unit/session_cookie_domain_test.php and SX-213's tests/unit/private_cache_headers_test.php stay green.

STEP 6 — docs (last): docs/ARCHITECTURE.md (lazy session on lnks.page; how it sits with SX-213's rule), web/Lnks.page/README.md; note that view counts can read slightly low because of browser caching; handoff.

VERIFY: php -l; php tests/run.php, exit code read directly; integration if a database is available; reason through a POST to every lnks.page route and state in the commit what was not run on Apache.
acceptance_criteria: lnks.page starts no session for a plain GET; every form or POST path starts one first; other components unchanged; SX-213's no-store rule for signed-in requests still holds
Plain, ungated, unprotected, form-free views send Cache-Control public for linkspage.public_cache_seconds (seeded 60); everything else, and any response carrying a cookie, sends private, no-store
The cache decision is a pure, fully unit-tested function; setting seeded (seed 054)
Existing session and cache-header tests green; docs record the trade-off
LP-26.issue_comment: Owner decision (2026-09-21, #243 decision 41): public LinksPages may be cached by the visitor's browser for 60 seconds; pages with an age gate, a password or a form are never cached. Plan (LP-26): lnks.page starts a session only when a page needs one (a gate or a form), and plain views send 'public, max-age=60' (setting linkspage.public_cache_seconds; 0 turns it off). Any request with a signed-in user keeps the 'no-store, private' rule from #213, and a response that carries a cookie is never cached. The trade-off: an edit or unpublish can take up to a minute to show, and view counts can read slightly low. Built after the password, email sign-up, embed and click items so every case that must never be cached exists.

HK-01.new_issue_title: 🤝 [Process] Move the handoff to .github/HANDOFF.md and record owner decisions 16–19 in the working rules
HK-01.new_issue_body:
## What and why

Owner decision 17 (#243): the project's one handoff moves to `.github/HANDOFF.md`, as it is in MeedyaDL. Every AI session and every builder reads and writes it, so every pointer to it must change in the same commit. Otherwise the next session reads a file that is no longer kept up to date.

The same commit writes decisions 16, 18 and 19 into `.claude/memory/working-rules.md`:

- **16:** fact-gathering may run in parallel. Planning judgements are still made one agent after another.
- **18:** the dev-team plugin stays in use, and the project's stricter rules win where they differ. Its work never goes straight onto the working branch, always goes through the cross-system review loop and the one-issue-one-commit format, and it never pushes.
- **19:** the plugin's files live under `docs/` (moved by a separate issue).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `.claude/HANDOFF.md` moved to `.github/HANDOFF.md` with `git mv`.
- [ ] Every reference updated: CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, `.claude/README.md`, `.claude/memory/*`, the sync script comments, docs.
- [ ] Working rules updated for decisions 16–19.
- [ ] `.OpenAI/` refreshed; `scripts/sync-ai-context.sh --check` passes.
- [ ] Only historical log lines still mention the old path.

## Dependencies

Built first in the merged order, straight after the four in-flight items have committed. Relates to #243 and #202.

HK-02.new_issue_title: 🗂️ [Process] Move the dev-team plugin's files under docs/dev-team/ and add a proper vulnerability-reporting policy
HK-02.new_issue_body:
## What and why

Owner decision 19 (#243): the dev-team plugin's own files (`PROJECT.md`, `FEATURES.md`, `SECURITY.md` at the repository root, and `.dev-team/autopilot.json`) move under `docs/` and stay tracked.

Two reasons. The plugin rewrites these files at the root whenever it runs, which would compete with the project's own records. And a root `SECURITY.md` is what GitHub shows as the project's security policy, but today that file is the plugin's old findings register, not a way to report a vulnerability.

Owner decision 36: security problems are reported through GitHub's private vulnerability reporting (the owner switches it on) and through an in-app security report form (built separately). The new policy names both.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The four files moved to `docs/dev-team/` with history kept, plus a short README explaining what they are.
- [ ] Fresh copies the plugin writes at the root are ignored by git.
- [ ] Links to and inside the moved files still work.
- [ ] `.github/SECURITY.md`: a short, plain-English policy naming both reporting routes.
- [ ] The pre-launch checklist tells the owner how to switch on private vulnerability reporting.
- [ ] `.dev-team/config.yml` comments updated; its settings unchanged.

## Dependencies

The handoff move (HK-01).

SX-196.title: Test and production databases use the right collation: CI fix, installer check, collation-proof stored procedures, a migration, and the collation written into every developer document
SX-196.plan:
GOAL: #196. The integration suite has been failing unseen, and a panel-created production database could break every link creation. Three causes, three fixes, plus making the integration job count. Decisions 32 and 33 (#243 second set) add: the required collation (utf8mb4_unicode_ci) is stated in DEV_NOTES.md and the other developer documentation; the pre-launch checklist gets a manual 'check the live database's collation' step; and the owner gets exact steps to make the integration tests a required check once they pass on this branch's pull request.

STEP 1 — CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml, job tests-integration):
(a) Remove MYSQL_DATABASE from the mysql service env, so schema/000_create_database.sql creates the database with utf8mb4_unicode_ci. Comment why: the container pre-created it with the server default utf8mb4_0900_ai_ci, and CREATE DATABASE IF NOT EXISTS then silently kept that.
(b) Add a step after the import, 'Check database collation': a mysql query of SELECT DEFAULT_COLLATION_NAME FROM information_schema.SCHEMATA WHERE SCHEMA_NAME='mwtools_Go2MyLink' that fails the step (exit 1) unless the result is exactly utf8mb4_unicode_ci.
(c) Remove continue-on-error: true from BOTH the job (line 197) and the step 'PHP integration tests (advisory)' (line 276). Rename the step to 'PHP integration tests'. KEEP the job name 'Tests (Integration)' and the single-value matrix os: [ubuntu-latest] (patterns.md rule: that matrix produces the check name 'Tests (Integration) (ubuntu-latest)'). Rewrite the job's header comment: it is now meant to pass; making it a REQUIRED check is an owner step (decision 33) described in docs/DEPLOYMENT.md.
(d) .github/workflows/mariadb-import.yml already starts MariaDB with --collation-server=utf8mb4_unicode_ci. Leave it, but add the same collation check step after its import.

STEP 2 — installer (web/Go2My.Link/public_html/install/index.php). In the 'test database connection' action (~lines 732-765), after a successful connect, query SELECT DEFAULT_CHARACTER_SET_NAME, DEFAULT_COLLATION_NAME FROM information_schema.SCHEMATA WHERE SCHEMA_NAME = ? (prepared, with the entered name). If it is not utf8mb4 / utf8mb4_unicode_ci: try ALTER DATABASE `<name>` CHARACTER SET utf8mb4 COLLATE utf8mb4_unicode_ci, first validating the name against ^[A-Za-z0-9_$-]{1,64}$ and refusing anything else (an identifier cannot be a bound parameter). Re-check. If it still does not match, refuse to move to the import step with a plain error that shows the exact SQL to run in the hosting panel and explains why: text comparisons inside the stored procedures fail with a different collation, and every short-link creation would fail (#196, #197).

STEP 3 — stored procedures, so they no longer depend on the database default. In web/_sql/procedures/sp_generateShortCode.sql and sp_lookupShortURL.sql, every comparison between a routine variable or parameter and a table column gets an explicit collation on the variable side, e.g. WHERE shortCode = v_candidate COLLATE utf8mb4_unicode_ci AND orgHandle = inputOrgHandle COLLATE utf8mb4_unicode_ci. Read the whole of sp_lookupShortURL to find every such comparison (domain, code, orgHandle, alias chains, fallback lookups). Use the expression-level COLLATE clause, which works on both MySQL 8 and MariaDB; do NOT add COLLATE to parameter declarations (MariaDB support unconfirmed). Header comment in each file: why (#196), and that the database itself should still be utf8mb4_unicode_ci. Do not touch the EXIT HANDLERs; SX-197 does that.

STEP 4 — existing databases: new migration web/_sql/migrations/042_database_collation.sql (header in the style of migration 021): USE `mwtools_Go2MyLink`; ALTER DATABASE CHARACTER SET utf8mb4 COLLATE utf8mb4_unicode_ci; (no name, so it applies to the current database). Header: it needs the ALTER privilege (if refused, change it in the hosting panel instead); tables are unaffected because each states its own collation; stored procedures remember the collation that was current when they were created, so AFTER this migration re-import web/_sql/procedures/sp_generateShortCode.sql and sp_lookupShortURL.sql. Idempotent. Add the collation line to schema/000_create_database.sql's comment (no code change there).

STEP 5 — tests: tests/integration/database_collation_test.php (DB guards copied from tests/integration/entitlements_test.php lines 60-80): the test database's default collation is utf8mb4_unicode_ci; every table in the schema has TABLE_COLLATION utf8mb4_unicode_ci (information_schema.TABLES); a CALL to sp_generateShortCode for '[default]' returns a non-empty code. tests/unit/ci_workflow_test.php (static): ci.yml contains no 'MYSQL_DATABASE', the tests-integration job has no 'continue-on-error: true', and the job keeps 'os: [ubuntu-latest]' (simple string checks, no YAML library). tests/unit/collation_docs_test.php (static): DEV_NOTES.md, docs/DATABASE.md, docs/INSTALL.md, docs/DEPLOYMENT.md and .claude/memory/patterns.md each contain 'utf8mb4_unicode_ci'.

STEP 6 — documentation (last, one builder at a time), decision 32:
(a) DEV_NOTES.md: a new section '🔤 Database collation (required)': the database, every table and every text column use utf8mb4 with the collation utf8mb4_unicode_ci; in plain words what a collation is (the rules for comparing and sorting text); why it matters here (comparisons inside the stored procedures take the database's collation, and a mismatch makes every short-link creation fail — #196, #197); the check query; how to fix a wrong database (migration 042 or the hosting panel, then re-import both procedure files); that CI and the installer now enforce it; that every new CREATE TABLE must state ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4 COLLATE=utf8mb4_unicode_ci.
(b) The same rule, briefly, with a link to that section, in: README.md's developer or setup section (if it has one), docs/DATABASE.md (under the character set / collation table), docs/INSTALL.md (the existing box: the installer now checks and corrects this), docs/DEPLOYMENT.md, and .claude/memory/patterns.md (database conventions). Then run sh scripts/sync-ai-context.sh and sh scripts/sync-ai-context.sh --check, reading the exit code directly, so .OpenAI/ matches.
(c) PRE_LAUNCH_CHECKLIST.md: rewrite A8 as a manual check with two moments: (1) before the first import on the live database and (2) again immediately before launch, on the live database: run SELECT DEFAULT_COLLATION_NAME FROM information_schema.SCHEMATA WHERE SCHEMA_NAME='mwtools_Go2MyLink'; expect exactly utf8mb4_unicode_ci; if not, run migration 042 (or change it in the panel) and re-import both procedure files, then re-run the query. Keep its 🔴 marker.
(d) Decision 33, exact owner steps, in docs/DEPLOYMENT.md and as a row in PRE_LAUNCH_CHECKLIST.md's 'Manual actions' table: 'Once the check "Tests (Integration) (ubuntu-latest)" has passed on this branch''s pull request: GitHub → the repository → Settings → Rules → Rulesets → "Protect main branch" → Edit → under "Require status checks to pass" choose "Add checks" → type Tests (Integration) (ubuntu-latest) → select it → Save changes. The name must match exactly. (Menu labels may differ slightly; the check name must not.)'
(e) Handoff.

VERIFY: php -l install/index.php; php tests/run.php, exit code read directly. If a local MySQL is available, import schema, procedures and seeds into a database pre-created with utf8mb4_0900_ai_ci and confirm the procedure still works (proving step 3), then run php tests/run_integration.php. State plainly in the commit what could not be run.

STEP 1 — web/_sql/procedures/sp_generateShortCode.sql: delete the DECLARE EXIT HANDLER FOR SQLEXCEPTION block (lines 42–46). SX-206.title: API key expiry fails safe: an unreadable expiry date means expired
SX-206.plan:
GOAL: #206. An expiry the code cannot read must refuse the key, not wave it through.

STEP 1 — web/_functions/api_auth.php: add a PURE function near the key verifier:
/** ... Returns true when the key must be treated as expired. A NULL expiry means the key never expires. An expiry strtotime() cannot read is treated as expired, because a security check must refuse when it is unsure (#206); the export-download check in data_rights.php already does this. */
function g2ml_apiKeyIsExpired(?string $expiresAt, int $nowTimestamp): bool
{ if ($expiresAt === null || trim($expiresAt) === '') { return false; } $ts = strtotime($expiresAt); if ($ts === false) { return true; } if ($ts < $nowTimestamp) { return true; } return false; }
Decision: an empty string is treated like NULL, because the column is nullable DATETIME and '' can only come from a hand edit; comment it. If you disagree after reading how the column is written, treat '' as expired instead and say so in the commit. Replace the block at lines ~371–379 with: if (g2ml_apiKeyIsExpired($row['expiresAt'] === null ? ... — no: write it with full if/else and a local variable, since there is no ternary rule. $expiresAtValue = null; if ($row['expiresAt'] !== null) { $expiresAtValue = (string) $row['expiresAt']; } if (g2ml_apiKeyIsExpired($expiresAtValue, time())) { return null; }.

STEP 2 — web/Go2My.Link/_admin/public_html/pages/api-keys/index.php lines ~357–366: compute $isExpired with the same function, so an unreadable date shows 'Expired'.

STEP 3 — tests/unit/api_auth_test.php: add cases null → false; '' → false; '2000-01-01 00:00:00' → true; a date 1 day ahead of a fixed now → false; 'not a date' → true; '0000-00-00 00:00:00' → true (strtotime gives a large negative number, which is in the past; assert it).

VERIFY: php -l both files; php tests/run.php exit 0.
acceptance_criteria: g2ml_apiKeyIsExpired() treats an unreadable expiry as expired and NULL as never-expiring (unit tests)
API authentication refuses such a key and the keys page shows it as Expired
php tests/run.php exits 0; no shorthand syntax
SX-206.issue_comment: Planned on 2026-09-21 (owner decision 21, #243). A new pure function, g2ml_apiKeyIsExpired(), is used by both API authentication and the keys page. An expiry date the code cannot read is now treated as expired (refused, shown as 'Expired'), the same as the export-download check; a missing expiry still means the key never expires. Unit tests cover an unreadable value, a zero date, past and future dates. Planner key SX-206.

SX-207.title: CSS cleaner strips backslash escapes before its keyword checks
SX-207.plan:
GOAL: #207, the simplest safe option. Browsers decode CSS backslash escapes (\69 = i), so '@\69mport' is a real @import that the literal keyword checks miss. Remove every backslash before the checks run. This must land before LP-29 (user templates) is ever switched on. STEP 1 — web/_functions/html_sanitiser.php _g2ml_htmlSanitiserCleanCssTokens() (line ~420): straight after the control-character removal and BEFORE comment stripping, add $clean = str_replace('\\', '', $clean); (a single backslash character in the PHP source: '\\'). Comment block: why (the browser decodes \hh escapes, so '@\69mport', 'e\78pression(' and 'u\72l(' used to pass, #207); why stripping rather than decoding (decoding CSS escapes correctly is fiddly and a mistake re-opens the hole, while legitimate page CSS almost never needs a backslash); the one known cost (content: "\201C" style escapes stop working; the character itself can be typed instead); and that the result is stable when cleaned again (removing backslashes twice changes nothing), which the existing re-sanitisation check relies on. This one function covers both the stylesheet path (g2ml_sanitiseUserCSS) and inline style attributes. An HTML entity such as \ inside a style attribute has already been decoded to a backslash by the DOM parser, so it is caught too. STEP 2 — docblocks: the g2ml_sanitiseUserCSS() docblock and the file header list 'backslashes removed' among the rules. docs: the custom HTML section in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md (or wherever the sanitiser rules are documented; grep 'sanitiseUserCSS' in docs), one line. STEP 3 — tests/unit/html_sanitiser_test.php, add: "@\69mport url('https://evil.example/x.css');" → no '@import' and no 'evil.example' import survives (assert the output does not contain '@import' case-insensitively and does not contain '\\'); 'width: e\78pression(alert(1));' → contains 'blocked(' and no 'expression('; 'background: u\72l(javascript:alert(1));' → the url is neutralised (output contains 'none' or 'blocked:' and never 'javascript:'); an inline style attribute through g2ml_sanitiseUserHTML('

x

') → no 'javascript:'; stability: cleaning the cleaned output again gives the same string. VERIFY: php -l; php tests/run.php exit 0.
acceptance_criteria: Every backslash is removed from user CSS (stylesheets and inline style attributes) before the keyword and url() checks
The four escaped attacks from the issue and an entity-encoded inline style are neutralised (unit tests); cleaning twice gives the same result
The known cost (escaped characters in content: strings) is documented; php tests/run.php exits 0
SX-207.issue_comment: Planned on 2026-09-21 (owner decision 21, #243), using the simplest safe option: every backslash is removed from user CSS before the keyword checks. This covers both custom stylesheets and inline style attributes, including \ entities, which the HTML parser has already decoded. The one cost is that escaped characters in CSS content strings stop working; the character itself can be typed instead. The four cases from this issue are added as unit tests, plus a stability check (cleaning twice changes nothing). This lands before user-uploaded templates (LP-29) can be switched on. SX-212.title: Rate-limit registration, contact and password-reset forms with a counter Do Not Track cannot bypass; send the contact form through g2ml_sendEmail
SX-212.plan:
GOAL: #212. A visitor who sends DNT is therefore never limited. All three forms move to a small attempts table that stores only a keyed hash of the IP address.

STEP 1 — schema: web/_sql/schema/044_form_attempts.sql, table tblFormAttempts: attemptUID BIGINT UNSIGNED AUTO_INCREMENT PK; formKey VARCHAR(40) NOT NULL COMMENT 'which form: register, contact, password_reset'; ipHash CHAR(64) NOT NULL COMMENT 'keyed hash of the visitor IP address, never the address itself'; createdAt DATETIME NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP; INDEX IDX_form_attempts_lookup (formKey, ipHash, createdAt); INDEX IDX_form_attempts_created (createdAt); InnoDB utf8mb4_unicode_ci. Plain-English header: why a hash, why not tblActivityLog, and that rows older than a day are deleted. Migration web/_sql/migrations/043_form_attempts.sql: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS with the same body (header in the style of migration 021).

STEP 2 — web/_functions/form_rate_limit.php (new, functions only, new-style guard per design note 5; loaded from page_init.php next to the security functions, with a guarded require_once and a file_exists check like the pricing.php block): g2ml_formRateLimitIpHash(): string = hash_hmac('sha256', g2ml_getClientIP(), ENCRYPTION_KEY_SECONDARY . '|form-attempt'). If the constant is missing, use '' as the key and error_log once. g2ml_formRateLimitCount(string $formKey, int $windowSeconds): int (prepared COUNT with createdAt >= DATE_SUB(UTC_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL ? SECOND); on a database failure return PHP_INT_MAX so the caller refuses, which fails closed; documented). g2ml_formRateLimitRecord(string $formKey): void (INSERT; then with random_int(1, 50) === 1 DELETE FROM tblFormAttempts WHERE createdAt < DATE_SUB(UTC_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 1 DAY) LIMIT 500). g2ml_formRateLimitExceeded(string $formKey, int $maxPerHour): bool (maxPerHour <= 0 means no limit, which is only possible by setting it on purpose). formKey whitelist: 'register', 'contact', 'password_reset'; anything else is error_logged and treated as exceeded.

STEP 3 — settings and strings: web/_sql/seeds/057_form_rate_limit_settings.sql (ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE settingDescription only for settings; INSERT IGNORE for translations; header noting it is applied to existing databases as-is). Settings, scope 'System', integer, editable: security.register_max_per_ip_per_hour '10' ('Most new accounts one IP address may create in an hour. Offices and schools share one address, so do not set this too low. 0 means no limit.'); security.contact_max_per_ip_per_hour '5'; security.password_reset_max_per_ip_per_hour '5'. Translation register.error_rate_limit 'Too many sign-ups from your network in the last hour. Please try again later.' (en-GB, context 'Registration page').

STEP 4 — registration (web/Go2My.Link/public_html/pages/register/index.php): after the CSRF and CAPTCHA checks pass and before registerUser() (line ~110): if g2ml_formRateLimitExceeded('register', (int) getSetting('security.register_max_per_ip_per_hour', 10)) → show __('register.error_rate_limit') with the English fallback, and logActivity('rate_limited', 'failed', 429, ['logData' => ['form' => 'register']]) ('rate_limited' is on the always-log list); else g2ml_formRateLimitRecord('register') and continue. Record every attempt that reaches registerUser(), successful or not, so repeated invalid attempts also count.

STEP 5 — forgot-password (pages/forgot-password/index.php lines ~91–115): replace the tblActivityLog COUNT with g2ml_formRateLimitExceeded('password_reset', setting) and record the attempt. Keep the existing message. Comment the DNT bypass that this closes.

STEP 6 — contact (pages/contact/index.php lines ~120–200): the same limit with 'contact', recorded only when a message is actually handed to the mailer. Replace the raw @mail() with g2ml_sendEmail($recipient, $subject, 'contact_message', ['contactName' => ..., 'contactEmail' => ..., 'contactSubject' => ..., 'contactMessage' => ...], '', ['Reply-To' => $contactEmail]). Do NOT put the visitor's IP address in the email any more (data minimisation; comment it). The logActivity('contact_form', ...) data drops 'senderEmail' and keeps only whether a subject was given ('hasSubject' => bool). The email address is personal data and is no longer needed for the rate limit.

STEP 7 — web/_functions/email.php g2ml_sendEmail(): (a) Reply-To override: before building headers, if $extraHeaders has a key matching 'reply-to' case-insensitively whose value passes filter_var(FILTER_VALIDATE_EMAIL) after CR/LF stripping, use it as $replyTo and remove it from $extraHeaders; an invalid value is dropped with an error_log line. (b) Test seam: if isset($GLOBALS['g2ml_email_send_override']) and is_callable, call it with ($to, $subject, $emailBody, $headers) instead of mail() and use its bool result. Document it as a test seam only; LP-18 reuses it (design note 6).

STEP 8 — tests. tests/unit/form_rate_limit_test.php: the whitelist refusal (unknown formKey → exceeded) through a pure helper g2ml_formRateLimitKeyIsValid(); the hash is 64 hex characters and differs for two REMOTE_ADDR values. tests/unit/email_reply_to_test.php using the seam: a valid Reply-To replaces the default (exactly one 'Reply-To:' line in the captured headers); an address containing CR/LF is dropped. tests/integration/form_rate_limit_test.php (DB guards): record 3 → count 3; a different IP (change $_SERVER['REMOTE_ADDR']) → 0; the limit refuses at the max; old rows are ignored by the window. tests/integration/auth_register_test.php: add a case where the 11th registration from one IP within an hour is refused, calling the same helper the page uses (the page itself is not unit-loadable).

STEP 9 — docs: docs/DATABASE.md (new table, three settings), PRE_LAUNCH_CHECKLIST.md (CAPTCHA keys still recommended; the limits are the floor), handoff.

VERIFY: php -l on every touched PHP file; php tests/run.php exit 0; integration if a DB is available; import schema 044 and migration 043 twice.
acceptance_criteria: tblFormAttempts (schema 044, migration 043) stores only a keyed hash of the IP; rows older than a day are removed
Registration, contact and forgot-password are limited per IP per hour from settings (seed 057), and the limit applies to Do-Not-Track visitors too; a database fault refuses rather than allows
The contact form sends through g2ml_sendEmail with a proper Reply-To and no longer puts the sender's IP in the email or their email address in the activity log
g2ml_sendEmail supports a validated Reply-To override and a documented send test seam

SX-212.issue_comment: Planned on 2026-09-21 (owner decision 21, #243). SX-213.title: Admin site not indexed, signed-in pages never cached, and all three service workers keep only static files
SX-213.plan:
GOAL: #213, with its scope DECIDED by decision 43 (#243 second set): the go2my.link and lnks.page service workers, not only the admin one, stop saving whole pages. On lnks.page, saved pages would keep password-protected pages (LP-13) readable offline. This must land before LP-13.

STEP 1 — robots on the admin site. web/_includes/header.php line 120: emit <meta name='robots' content='noindex, nofollow'> when defined('G2ML_COMPONENT') && G2ML_COMPONENT === 'Admin', otherwise keep 'index, follow' (full if/else). web/Go2My.Link/_admin/public_html/.htaccess: add Header always set X-Robots-Tag "noindex, nofollow" in the headers block, with a comment. New web/Go2My.Link/_admin/public_html/robots.txt: 'User-agent: *' / 'Disallow: /'. Confirm the admin .htaccess serves existing files directly (a RewriteCond -f before routing); if not, add an exception for robots.txt and offline.html.

STEP 2 — no caching of signed-in pages. web/_functions/security.php: PURE g2ml_privatePageCacheHeaders(bool $isSignedIn, string $component): array returns ['Cache-Control' => 'no-store, private', 'Pragma' => 'no-cache'] when $isSignedIn is true OR $component === 'Admin'; otherwise []. web/_includes/page_init.php, right after the session-validation block (~line 420), when headers are not yet sent: $isSignedIn = isset($_SESSION['user_uid']) && (int) $_SESSION['user_uid'] > 0; loop over the returned headers and call header(name . ': ' . value). Comment: a later header() with the same name replaces this (the API and the export downloads already send no-store); LP-26's public caching on lnks.page applies only to requests with no session (fixes design note 8).

STEP 3 — service workers: web/Go2My.Link/_admin/public_html/sw.js, web/Go2My.Link/public_html/sw.js and web/Lnks.page/public_html/sw.js. The same change in each:
- CACHE_NAME bumps to '-v2' (go2mylink-admin-v2, go2mylink-v2, lnkspage-v2). The existing activate handler then deletes the v1 caches that hold saved pages; comment that this is deliberate.
- APP_SHELL no longer contains '/'. It holds the icons, manifest.json and '/offline.html'.
- In the fetch handler, static assets (the existing pattern) keep cache-first. Navigations and every other request are network-only: event.respondWith(fetch(request).catch(function () { return caches.match('/offline.html'); })) for request.mode === 'navigate', and no respondWith at all for other non-static requests. No cache.put on any HTML response. Full braces, no arrow functions, no ternaries (house JS rule).
- A comment at the top: why HTML is never saved (private pages stayed readable after sign-out on shared computers, #213; on lnks.page, password-protected pages; decision 43 extends it to all three).
New static web/Go2My.Link/_admin/public_html/offline.html, web/Go2My.Link/public_html/offline.html and web/Lnks.page/public_html/offline.html: a minimal accessible page (lang='en-GB', a title, one heading 'You are offline', one sentence 'Check your connection and try again.', a link to '/' labelled 'Try again', inline CSS using prefers-color-scheme for dark mode, no scripts, no external resources). SX-203.title: Automated check that no web address in shipping code ends in .php
SX-203.plan:
GOAL: #203 and the owner's standing rule. A unit test in tests/unit, run by tests/run.php and therefore by CI's must-pass 'PHP unit tests' step, fails when any shipping web address ends in .php.

STEP 1 — tests/unit/no_php_in_urls_test.php (DB-free, pure PHP, no new tools). File header: the rule, the two reasons (it tells strangers what the site is built with, and such links are often silently broken), and the owner's reference implementation idea.
- Files scanned: RecursiveDirectoryIterator over web/, with extensions .php, .js, .html, .htm and files named .htaccess. Skipped folders: any path segment named _libraries, _backups or _uploads, plus web/_sql and web/_schemas, which are not web pages. Everything else is scanned, including public_html_landing, public_html_redir, private_html, _admin and the installer.
- Patterns (case-insensitive; the matched address is the captured group):
  (1) HTML attributes: \b(?:href|action|src|formaction)\s*=\s*["']([^"'\s>]*?\.php)(?:[?#][^"']*)?["']
  (2) PHP redirects: header\(\s*["']Location:\s*([^"']*?\.php)(?:[?#][^"']*)?["']
  (3) JavaScript requests and navigation: (?:fetch|open|location(?:\.href)?\s*=|location\.(?:assign|replace))\s*\(?\s*(?:["'][A-Z]+["']\s*,\s*)?["'`]([^"'`\s]*?\.php)(?:[?#][^"'`]*)?["'`]
  (4) .htaccess external redirects: a RewriteRule line whose target ends in .php (optionally followed by a query string) AND whose flags contain R or R=3xx, or a Redirect/RedirectMatch line whose target ends in .php. Internal RewriteRule targets such as index.php are file paths, not addresses, and are NOT flagged. Comment why.
- Lines whose first non-space characters are //, #, * or <!-- are skipped. A match is ignored when the captured value has no '/' and no '.php' preceded by a letter, which filters out regex fragments; keep this heuristic small and explain it.
- Allow-list: a short constant array of ['file' => relative path, 'match' => exact string, 'reason' => plain English]. Start it empty. Add an entry only for a real false positive found in step 2, with its reason.
- Failure message: one line per finding, 'path:line: <matched address>', so the fix is obvious.
- Self-test: run the matcher functions (write them as small named functions inside the test file, prefixed _g2mlNoPhpTest…) against built-in sample strings: '<a href="/help/api/index.php">' flagged; '<a href="/help/api">' not flagged; "header('Location: /login.php?x=1')" flagged; "require_once __DIR__ . '/x.php';" not flagged; "fetch('/api/create/index.php')" flagged; 'RewriteRule ^info/(.+)$ index.php?code=$1 [L]' not flagged; 'RewriteRule ^old$ /new.php [R=301,L]' flagged.

STEP 2 — run it on the current tree. A search on 2026-09-21 found no offenders; if it finds any, fix each real one in shipping code in this same commit (point the link at the clean address the router registers) and list them in the commit body. Put anything that is not a web address on the allow-list with a reason.

STEP 3 — tests/README.md: a short section 'No .php in web addresses' explaining what the test checks, how to read a failure, and how to add an allow-list entry.

VERIFY: php tests/run.php and read the exit code directly; temporarily add a line with href="/x.php" to a scratch copy (not a tracked file) to confirm the matcher flags it, then delete the scratch file.
acceptance_criteria: tests/unit/no_php_in_urls_test.php scans shipping code under web/ (excluding _libraries, _backups, _uploads, _sql, _schemas) for href/action/src/formaction values, Location redirects, JavaScript requests and external .htaccess redirects ending in .php
Internal rewrite targets and require/include paths are not flagged; a built-in self-test proves both directions
Any offender found on the current tree is fixed in the same commit; the allow-list is empty or every entry has a reason
tests/README.md documents it; php tests/run.php exits 0 and CI runs it through the existing unit-test step
