PF-13.title: Personal plans for individuals: an invisible personal account holder, and one function that decides which plan applies to a person
PF-13.plan:
GOAL: owner decisions 25 and 26 (#243 second set). (25) People with no organisation (the shared '[default]' organisation) count as the Free plan; GlobalAdmins stay unlimited. (26) An individual can have a paid plan in their own name without joining an organisation, through an invisible personal account holder: they never see or manage an 'organisation', and the existing plan machinery and the tier admin work unchanged.

IMPORTANT FACT FROM THE CODE: '[default]' is also where every anonymous (not signed-in) short link lives (shorturl_create.php line 543 defaults to it). If '[default]' itself became Free, every anonymous visitor would share one 50-link allowance. So the '[default]' unlimited answer in _g2ml_resolveOrgTier() STAYS, but from now on it is reached only by anonymous and system flows and by GlobalAdmins. Every check made on behalf of a PERSON first maps that person to the right plan holder through one function, g2ml_entitlementOrgHandleForUser(). The call sites are switched over by later items (PF-08 for links, statistics and the API; PF-10 for the statistics window; LP-27 for LinksPages). This item builds the function, the personal holder and what the person sees.

DESIGN
- Individuals stay in '[default]': tblUsers.orgHandle is not changed, so their links, LinksPages and API keys keep their current scope, and createOrganisation() and acceptInvitation(), which require '[default]', keep working.
- A personal account holder is an ordinary tblOrganisations row, created only when needed (lazily), never at sign-up. No row means Free (decision 25), so no backfill of existing users is needed. Handle: '[personal-<userUID>]'. The square brackets can never be produced by _g2ml_validateOrgHandle() (it allows only lowercase letters, digits and hyphens), so nobody can register or collide with it; the longest possible handle is 31 characters, under the 50-character column. orgName 'Personal account' (no name or email: data minimisation), isVerified 0, isActive 1, tierID = the fallback tier (lowest sortOrder active tier, today 'free') at creation, orgNotes 'Invisible personal account holder (#243 decision 26). Not shown to the person.'.
- New columns on tblOrganisations: isPersonal TINYINT(1) UNSIGNED NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 COMMENT 'This row is an individual''s invisible personal account holder (decision 26)'; personalOwnerUserUID BIGINT UNSIGNED NULL COMMENT 'The person this personal holder belongs to; NULL after account erasure'; UNIQUE KEY UQ_org_personal_owner (personalOwnerUserUID) (several NULLs are allowed). No foreign key to tblUsers: schema 012 is imported before tblUsers exists (013), so a constraint cannot be declared there, and erasure handles the link explicitly (step 4); say so in a column comment.
- Because the holder is a normal organisation row, PF-03's retire-with-replacement moves personal holders too, overrides (PF-05) work on them, and the pricing engine resolves them like any organisation.

STEP 1 — schema and migration. Edit web/_sql/schema/012_core_organisations.sql: the two columns after isActive and the unique key, with plain-English comments. New migration web/_sql/migrations/044_personal_accounts.sql (header in the style of migration 016): guarded ADD COLUMN for each column and a guarded ADD UNIQUE INDEX (throwaway procedures checking information_schema.COLUMNS and information_schema.STATISTICS, copied from migration 016 lines 50-77). Idempotent.

STEP 2 — web/_functions/entitlements.php: g2ml_entitlementOrgHandleForUser(int $userUID, string $orgHandle): string. Rules in this order, full if/else:
 1. $orgHandle is not '' and not '[default]' → return $orgHandle (an organisation member; the org's plan applies).
 2. $userUID <= 0 → return '[default]' (anonymous or system flows keep the existing unlimited answer; comment: anonymous link creation has its own hourly and daily limits).
 3. the user's role is 'GlobalAdmin' → return '[default]' (unlimited, decision 25).
 4. an active personal holder exists for the user → return its orgHandle.
 5. otherwise → return '' (no organisation row, so _g2ml_resolveOrgTier() falls back to the lowest-sortOrder active tier, which is Free).
 Rules 3 and 4 use ONE prepared query per user per request: SELECT u.role, o.orgHandle AS personalHandle FROM tblUsers u LEFT JOIN tblOrganisations o ON o.isPersonal = 1 AND o.personalOwnerUserUID = u.userUID AND o.isActive = 1 WHERE u.userUID = ? LIMIT 1. Request cache $GLOBALS['g2ml_entitlement_user_org_cache'][$userUID]. On a query failure return '' and error_log once (the downstream tier lookup keeps its own fail-open / fail-closed rules). Test seam: when $GLOBALS['g2ml_personal_account_lookup_override'] is callable, call it with the userUID instead of the database; it returns ['role' => string, 'personalHandle' => ?string] or false (failure). Extend g2ml_clearOrgTierCache() to also unset the user cache. Docblock in plain English: decisions 25 and 26; why '[default]' still means unlimited for anonymous use; which later items switch the call sites over; that GlobalAdmins in an organisation are also unlimited through the existing acting-context rule.

STEP 3 — new web/_functions/personal_account.php (functions only, new-style direct-access guard from SX-198; NOT loaded by page_init — the few callers require_once it, so no shared bootstrap file changes): PURE g2ml_personalAccountHandleFor(int $userUID): string ('[personal-' . $userUID . ']', or '' when <= 0); PURE g2ml_personalAccountIsPersonalHandle(string $handle): bool (^\[personal-[1-9][0-9]{0,19}\]$); g2ml_personalAccountGet(int $userUID): array|null|false (the holder row: orgHandle, tierID, isActive); g2ml_personalAccountEnsure(int $userUID): array{success, orgHandle, created, error, errorCode} — the user must exist and be active (SELECT isActive FROM tblUsers WHERE userUID = ?); tier = _g2ml_fetchFallbackTierRow()['tierID'] (fallback 'free' if that fails); INSERT INTO tblOrganisations (orgHandle, orgName, tierID, isVerified, isActive, orgNotes, isPersonal, personalOwnerUserUID) VALUES (?, 'Personal account', ?, 0, 1, ?, 1, ?) ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE isActive = 1, personalOwnerUserUID = VALUES(personalOwnerUserUID) (idempotent through UQ_org_handle; re-activates a holder only for an active user); clear caches; logActivity('personal_account_created', 'success', 200, ['userUID' => $userUID]) only when a row was created. g2ml_personalAccountDeactivate(mysqli $db, int $userUID): bool — for account erasure, on the caller's connection inside its transaction: UPDATE tblOrganisations SET isActive = 0, personalOwnerUserUID = NULL, orgName = 'Closed personal account' WHERE isPersonal = 1 AND personalOwnerUserUID = ? (the row is kept for billing and audit history but no longer points at the person). g2ml_personalPlanNameForUser(int $userUID, string $orgHandle): string — '' for organisation members (their plan is shown on the organisation page as today); otherwise the tierName of the holder's tier, or of the fallback tier when there is no holder. Setting the tier is NOT done here: PF-05 adds the audited admin screen, and the billing work (#59) will call g2ml_personalAccountEnsure() plus the same audited setter.

STEP 4 — existing flows.
(a) web/_functions/org.php: _g2ml_validateOrgHandle() refuses any handle that starts with '[' with 'This handle is reserved.' (belt and braces; comment why). createOrganisation() and acceptInvitation(): after moving the user, call g2ml_clearOrgTierCache() so the rest of the request uses the organisation's plan. No other change to their behaviour.
(b) web/_functions/data_rights.php g2ml_anonymiseUserData(): inside the existing transaction, require_once personal_account.php and call g2ml_personalAccountDeactivate($db, $userUID); comment the reason.
(c) Anything listing organisations must not show personal holders to non-GlobalAdmins: grep -rn 'FROM tblOrganisations' web --include='*.php' (excluding _libraries). For each query that returns a LIST (not a lookup of the user's own org), add AND isPersonal = 0, or, on a GlobalAdmin-only screen, label such rows 'Personal account (user #<personalOwnerUserUID>)'. List what was checked in the commit body.

STEP 5 — what the person sees (component A), never the word 'organisation' or the handle.
(a) web/Go2My.Link/_admin/public_html/pages/profile/index.php: for a user in '[default]', a 'Your plan' line: __('personal.plan_label') and the name from g2ml_personalPlanNameForUser(), with a link __('personal.see_plans') → https://go2my.link/pricing. Not shown to organisation members.
(b) The create-organisation page (pages/org/create/index.php) and the invitation page (web/Go2My.Link/public_html/pages/invite/index.php): when the signed-in person has an ACTIVE personal holder whose tier is not the fallback tier (a paid personal plan), show an info alert before the confirm button: __('personal.join_notice', ['plan' => name]).
(c) What happens when they later join a team: their tblUsers.orgHandle becomes the organisation, so rule 1 applies and the organisation's plan covers everything they do as a member. The personal holder is kept, unchanged and dormant (a future billing flow must keep billing it until they cancel — note on #59). Links and LinksPages they made as an individual keep orgHandle '[default]' (existing behaviour) and still count against their personal allowance, not the organisation's. If they leave or are removed (org.php sets them back to '[default]'), their personal plan applies again automatically.

PF-13.new_issue_title: 👤 [Pricing] Personal plans for individuals: an invisible personal account holder, and one rule for which plan applies to a person
PF-13.new_issue_body:
## What and why

Owner decisions 25 and 26 (#243, second set):

- **25:** people without an organisation count as the Free plan. Today they sit in the shared `[default]` organisation, which the plan checks never limit, so they get everything unlimited. GlobalAdmins stay unlimited.
- **26:** an individual can buy a paid plan in their own name without joining an organisation. This is built as an invisible personal account holder: they never see or manage an organisation, and the existing plan machinery and tier admin work unchanged.

`[default]` is also where every anonymous (not signed-in) link lives, so it cannot simply become Free: every anonymous visitor would share one allowance. Instead, every check made on behalf of a person goes through one new function that decides which plan applies:

1. an organisation member → the organisation's plan;
2. a GlobalAdmin, or anonymous use → unlimited (as today);
3. an individual with a personal plan → their personal holder's plan;
4. any other individual → Free.

The personal holder is an ordinary organisation row with a bracketed name nobody can register, created only when a person gets a paid plan. The person only sees 'Your plan' on their profile. If they later join a team, the team's plan applies while they are a member; their personal plan is kept and applies again if they leave.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Two new columns on `tblOrganisations` (schema 012 + migration 044).
- [ ] `g2ml_entitlementOrgHandleForUser()` with the four rules, cached per request, unit-tested.
- [ ] Functions to create a personal holder (at most one per person) and to close it on account erasure.
- [ ] 'Your plan' on the profile; a notice when a person with a paid personal plan creates or joins an organisation.
- [ ] Personal holders never appear in organisation lists shown to non-GlobalAdmins.
- [ ] Integration tests, including joining and leaving an organisation.

## What this does not do

It does not switch the existing checks over. That happens in the Free-tier issue (#209, links, statistics and API), the statistics-window issue and the LinksPage plan foundation. The admin screen for giving a person a plan is in the exceptions/audit admin issue. Billing (#59) will use the same functions.

## Dependencies

The direct-access guard fix (#198) for the new file's guard pattern.

SR-01.new_issue_title: 🛡️ [Security] In-app security report form with a GlobalAdmin inbox and notification emails
SR-01.new_issue_body:
## What and why

Owner decision 36 (#243, second set): security problems can be reported through GitHub's private vulnerability reporting (the owner switches it on) **and** through a form on the site. Reports are visible to GlobalAdmins in the admin area, and GlobalAdmins get notification emails.

## What this adds

- A public page at `/security/report`: a short form (summary, affected area, optional address, details, the reporter's view of how serious it is, and optional name and email for a reply).
- Protection: CSRF check, a hidden trap field for bots, a CAPTCHA when one is configured, and at most 5 reports per hour from one network.
- Privacy: nothing is stored beyond what the reporter types. No IP address, browser details or account link. The email is encrypted. Contact details are removed automatically a year after the report is closed.
- A GlobalAdmin inbox at `admin.go2my.link/security/reports` to read, update and close reports.
- Notification emails to every GlobalAdmin. They carry only a reference and a link, not the report text, so vulnerability details and personal data do not sit in mailboxes.
- `.github/SECURITY.md` and a standard `security.txt` pointing at both routes.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] New table (schema 045, migration 045) with no IP, user-agent or user-id column.
- [ ] Form with CSRF, rate limit, optional CAPTCHA and honeypot.
- [ ] Inbox restricted to GlobalAdmins on the server.
- [ ] Notification email without report content.
- [ ] Automatic removal of contact details after closing.
- [ ] Unit and integration tests; strings seeded.

## Dependencies

The form attempts table and email test seam (#212), the plan admin menu entry (PF-04), and the security policy file (HK-02).

LP-33.title: Hold a deleted LinksPage's address for 30 days on every deletion path (and on a rename)
LP-33.plan:
GOAL: #244 as decided by owner decision 42 (#243 second set): when a LinksPage is deleted, its address (lnks.page/<slug>) is held for 30 days before anyone — including its former owner — can claim it, on every deletion path. One extension, stated plainly in the issue: when an owner RENAMES a page's address, the old address is held for 30 days too, because a rename frees it in exactly the same way (the Verified badge already treats a rename as sensitive, LP-32). The hold keeps no personal data: only the address text and an expiry time.

STEP 1 — schema and migration. New web/_sql/schema/046_linkspage_slug_holds.sql: tblLinksPageSlugHolds (InnoDB, utf8mb4_unicode_ci — the SAME collation as tblLinksPages.slug, so 'MyPage' and 'mypage' are the same address, exactly as the UQ_page_slug key treats them): holdUID BIGINT UNSIGNED AUTO_INCREMENT PK; slug VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL (matches tblLinksPages.slug); heldUntil DATETIME NOT NULL COMMENT 'UTC; the address can be claimed again after this'; reason ENUM('deleted','erased','renamed') NOT NULL; createdAt DATETIME NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP; UNIQUE KEY UQ_slug_hold (slug); INDEX (heldUntil). No user id and no page id (comment: decision 42 and #244 — a hold needs only the address and an expiry). Migration web/_sql/migrations/046_linkspage_slug_holds.sql: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS with the same body.

STEP 2 — seed web/_sql/seeds/062_linkspage_slug_hold.sql: setting linkspage.slug_hold_days ('30', integer, Default scope, 'Days a deleted or renamed LinksPage address is held before anyone can use it again (decision 42). 0 turns the hold off.'); translations: linkspage.error_slug_held 'That address belonged to a page that was deleted or renamed recently, so it cannot be used yet. Please choose a different one.', linkspage.delete_hold_warning 'After deletion, this address cannot be used by anyone, including you, for {days} days.', linkspage.rename_hold_warning 'If you change the address, the old one cannot be used by anyone, including you, for {days} days.'

STEP 3 — web/_functions/linkspage_manage.php helpers (functions near the slug validator): PURE g2ml_linkspageSlugHoldDays(mixed $settingValue): int (clamp 0-365, default 30); g2ml_linkspageSlugHoldAdd(mysqli $db, string $slug, string $reason): bool — on the caller's connection: INSERT INTO tblLinksPageSlugHolds (slug, heldUntil, reason) VALUES (?, DATE_ADD(UTC_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL ? DAY), ?) ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE heldUntil = GREATEST(heldUntil, VALUES(heldUntil)), reason = VALUES(reason); does nothing and returns true when the hold days are 0; then, when random_int(1, 20) === 1, DELETE FROM tblLinksPageSlugHolds WHERE heldUntil < DATE_SUB(UTC_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 1 DAY) LIMIT 500 (lazy clean-up; no scheduled job needed; comment why). g2ml_linkspageSlugIsHeld(string $slug): bool — SELECT 1 FROM tblLinksPageSlugHolds WHERE slug = ? AND heldUntil > UTC_TIMESTAMP() LIMIT 1; a database failure returns TRUE (fail closed: refuse the claim rather than risk handing out a held address; comment it).

STEP 4 — every path that frees an address. Find them all first with grep -rn "DELETE FROM tblLinksPages" web and grep -rn "slug" in the UPDATE of g2ml_linkspageManageUpdatePage; on 2026-09-21 they are:
(a) Manual delete, g2ml_linkspageManageDeletePage(): wrap in a transaction on getDB(): SELECT slug FROM tblLinksPages WHERE pageUID = ? AND userUID = ? FOR UPDATE; if no row → the existing not-found result; SlugHoldAdd($db, $slug, 'deleted'); if that fails → rollback and return an error 'Could not delete the LinksPage. Please try again.' with errorCode 'hold_failed' (the page is kept rather than its address freed unprotected); then LP-16's media clean-up and the DELETE as today; commit. Keep every existing behaviour after that.
(b) Account erasure, data_rights.php g2ml_anonymiseUserData(): inside its existing transaction, BEFORE the DELETE FROM tblLinksPages: SELECT slug FROM tblLinksPages WHERE userUID = ?, and SlugHoldAdd($db, $slug, 'erased') for each. If a hold insert fails, error_log it and CONTINUE: erasure is a legal duty and outranks the hold (comment it). Update the existing #244 comment block in that function to say the hold now exists.
(c) Rename, g2ml_linkspageManageUpdatePage(): when the submitted slug differs from the stored slug (byte comparison), check SlugIsHeld(new slug) before the UPDATE; after a successful UPDATE call SlugHoldAdd for the OLD slug with reason 'renamed' (on getDB(); a failure is logged — the rename already happened).
(d) Any other DELETE or slug change the grep finds: apply the same rule and list it in the commit.

STEP 5 — every path that claims an address: g2ml_linkspageManageCreatePage() and the rename branch of UpdatePage call g2ml_linkspageSlugIsHeld() after the format and reserved-word checks and before the INSERT/UPDATE; held → ['success' => false, 'error' => <English text of linkspage.error_slug_held>, 'errorCode' => 'slug_held']. The message never says when the address becomes free and never mentions the previous owner.

STEP 6 — admin pages: the delete confirmation on pages/linkspage/index.php (and edit/index.php if it has a delete button) shows __('linkspage.delete_hold_warning', ['days' => n]); the slug field's help text on the edit page shows __('linkspage.rename_hold_warning', ['days' => n]); the create and edit pages map errorCode 'slug_held' to __('linkspage.error_slug_held').

STEP 7 — tests: tests/unit/linkspage_slug_hold_test.php (HoldDays clamping and the default). tests/integration/linkspage_slug_hold_test.php (DB guards): delete a page → another user creating the same slug gets slug_held; the same owner also gets slug_held; a different-case slug ('MYPAGE' after 'mypage') is held too; after setting heldUntil to the past with a direct UPDATE the slug can be claimed; erasure of a user with two pages holds both slugs; renaming holds the old slug and frees nothing early; with linkspage.slug_hold_days = 0 nothing is held; a hold insert failure on manual delete keeps the page (simulate with a slug longer than the column only if strict mode rejects it; otherwise use a test seam $GLOBALS['g2ml_slug_hold_fail_override']); the hold table contains no user or page id columns (information_schema check).

STEP 8 — docs (last): docs/DATABASE.md (the table, the rule, what it stores); PRE_LAUNCH_CHECKLIST.md: 'Legal review: the Terms mention that a deleted or renamed LinksPage address is held for 30 days, including from its former owner (#244)'; handoff. Close #244 when merged.

VERIFY: php -l on every touched file; php tests/run.php, exit code read directly; integration with a database; import schema 046 and migration 046 twice.
acceptance_criteria: tblLinksPageSlugHolds (schema 046, migration 046) stores only the address, an expiry and a reason; same collation as page addresses

Manual delete, account erasure and any other deletion path hold the address for linkspage.slug_hold_days (30); a rename holds the old address; manual delete refuses rather than freeing an address without a hold; erasure never fails because of a hold
Creating or renaming to a held address is refused with a generic message (errorCode slug_held) for everyone, including the former owner; a database failure refuses
The admin screens warn before delete and rename; expired holds are cleaned up lazily with no scheduled job
Integration tests cover every path; strings and setting seeded (seed 062); suites green
LP-33.issue_comment: Owner decision (2026-09-21, #243 decision 42): a deleted page's address is held for 30 days before anyone can claim it, on every deletion path. Plan (LP-33): a small table (tblLinksPageSlugHolds, schema 046, migration 046) stores only the address, an expiry time and the reason; no user or page id. Manual delete and account erasure both add a hold. Manual delete refuses if the hold cannot be written, rather than freeing the address unprotected. Erasure logs the problem and carries on, because erasure is a legal duty. Creating or renaming to a held address is refused with a message that says nothing about the previous owner or when it becomes free. The former owner is held out too, as the decision says 'anyone'. One extension: renaming a page's address also holds the old address for 30 days, because a rename frees it in the same way. The setting linkspage.slug_hold_days (30) controls the length. Expired holds are tidied up as new holds are written, so no scheduled job is needed. The Terms should mention the hold; that is on the legal-review list.

PF-14.title: Daily exchange rate for the pricing page's approximate figures: fetched by the scheduled job, stored with its date, never shown when missing or stale
PF-14.plan:
GOAL: owner decision 40 (#243 second set): the pricing page shows an 'approximately' figure in currencies other than GBP, USD and EUR (and in USD or EUR where no fixed price is set), labelled as charged in GBP, using a daily exchange rate fetched by the scheduled job. It is information only: the charged price never changes and real prices are never converted. This item fetches and stores the rate; PF-07 displays it.

RATE SOURCE (name and terms, for the owner): Frankfurter (https://frankfurter.dev), an open-source service that needs no account and no API key and publishes the European Central Bank's euro foreign-exchange reference rates, re-based to any base currency. The ECB publishes these once per working day (around 16:00 Central European Time), not at weekends or on TARGET holidays, and states they are for information purposes only; the ECB allows reuse with the source acknowledged. That matches our use (an informational figure with the source and date shown). Frankfurter publishes no usage limits for reasonable use; we call it at most once a day. NOT VERIFIED by the planner: the exact current address. The default setting is 'https://api.frankfurter.dev/v1/latest?base=GBP'. Before committing, the builder runs one curl against it and, if it does not answer with the shape below, uses 'https://api.frankfurter.app/latest?from=GBP' as the default instead and says which in the commit. The address is a setting, so the owner can switch to a self-hosted Frankfurter or another compatible service without a code change. Expected response shape: {"amount": 1.0, "base": "GBP", "date": "2026-09-18", "rates": {"AUD": 1.93, "CAD": 1.79, ...}}.

STEP 1 — schema and migration. New web/_sql/schema/047_exchange_rates.sql: tblExchangeRates (InnoDB, utf8mb4_unicode_ci, plain-English header: informational only, never used to charge anyone, latest rate per currency only): rateUID BIGINT UNSIGNED AUTO_INCREMENT PK; baseCurrency CHAR(3) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'GBP'; quoteCurrency CHAR(3) NOT NULL; rate DECIMAL(18,8) NOT NULL COMMENT 'units of quoteCurrency for 1 baseCurrency'; rateDate DATE NOT NULL COMMENT 'the date the source says the rate is for'; source VARCHAR(40) NOT NULL; fetchedAt DATETIME NOT NULL COMMENT 'UTC'; UNIQUE KEY UQ_fx_pair (baseCurrency, quoteCurrency). Migration web/_sql/migrations/047_exchange_rates.sql: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS with the same body.

STEP 2 — settings: seed web/_sql/seeds/063_exchange_rate_settings.sql (ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE settingDescription only; header notes it is applied to existing databases as-is), scope System: pricing.fx_enabled ('1', boolean, 'Fetch a daily exchange rate used ONLY for approximate prices on the pricing page (decision 40). Never used to charge anyone.'); pricing.fx_source_url (the verified default above, string, 'Address of a Frankfurter-compatible service returning ECB reference rates with GBP as the base. Must start with https://.'); pricing.fx_max_age_days ('5', integer, 'If the stored rate is older than this many days, the approximate figure is simply not shown. The ECB does not publish at weekends or on holidays, so 5 covers a long weekend.'); pricing.fx_last_status ('', string, not editable, 'Written by the job: ok <date> or error <reason>.').

STEP 3 — web/_functions/fx_rates.php (new, functions only, new-style guard; required by cron.php's job and by pricing.php's display helpers, guarded by file_exists): PURE g2ml_fxValidateResponse(mixed $decoded, string $todayUtc, int $maxAgeDays): array{ok, date, rates, error} — must be an array with base === 'GBP' (case-sensitive), date matching ^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$ and a real calendar date, not later than today (UTC) and not older than $maxAgeDays, rates an array of at most 60 entries whose keys match ^[A-Z]{3}$ and are not 'GBP', and whose values are int or float with 0 < value < 1000000; anything else → ok false with a short reason ('bad_base', 'bad_date', 'stale', 'bad_rates'); PURE g2ml_fxShouldFetch(?string $lastFetchedAtUtc, string $nowUtc): bool — true when there is no previous fetch or it is at least 20 hours old (so a frequent trigger still fetches only once a day); g2ml_fxFetchRaw(string $url): string|false — refuse any URL not starting with https://; file_get_contents with stream_context_create(['http' => ['timeout' => 10, 'ignore_errors' => true, 'header' => 'User-Agent: Go2My.Link exchange-rate job' . "\r\n" . 'Accept: application/json']]) (the same approach as verifyCaptcha in shorturl_create.php); read at most 65536 bytes; a non-200 status in $http_response_header → false; test seam: when $GLOBALS['g2ml_fx_fetch_override'] is callable, return its result instead of making a request; g2ml_fxGetRate(string $quoteCurrency): ?array{rate: string, date: string} — null when the code is not ^[A-Z]{3}$, when no row exists, when rate <= 0, when rateDate is older than pricing.fx_max_age_days (UTC), or on any error; request-cached. PURE g2ml_fxApproximate(string $gbpAmount, string $rate, int $decimals): string — the GBP amount times the rate rounded to $decimals (a float is acceptable here because the figure is explicitly approximate; say so), returned as a plain number string.

STEP 4 — the job, web/_functions/cron.php: g2ml_cronNormaliseJobName() accepts 'exchange_rates'; g2ml_cronRunJobs(): 'all' runs it LAST (after retention), because it is the least important job. g2ml_cronRunExchangeRateJob(): array — gated by getSetting('pricing.fx_enabled', false) === true; skipped (report skipped: 'fresh') when g2ml_fxShouldFetch(MAX(fetchedAt), now) is false; otherwise fetch pricing.fx_source_url, json_decode, validate, and in ONE transaction upsert every rate (INSERT ... ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE rate, rateDate, source = 'frankfurter-ecb', fetchedAt = UTC_TIMESTAMP()); write pricing.fx_last_status 'ok <date>' through setSetting. On ANY failure: leave the stored rows untouched, write 'error <reason>', error_log one line; the pricing page then hides approximate figures once the rows go stale (fail safe). Report {enabled, fetched, skipped, date, count, error}. The job never runs from the 1-in-500 page-load fallback (an outside request must never slow a visitor's page); it runs only when the scheduled trigger calls the endpoint with job=all or job=exchange_rates, which needs #198 (SX-198, landed) and the #178 trigger. Until the trigger is wired there is no rate, and the page shows no approximate figures (state this in the docs). Update the job list in the cron endpoint's docblock.

STEP 5 — admin visibility: on pages/platform/index.php (PF-04/PF-05/PF-06), one line in the engine panel: 'Exchange rate for approximate prices: <pricing.fx_last_status or "never fetched">' through __('tieradmin.fx_status', ['status' => ...]) (add the key to seed 063 as an INSERT IGNORE translation).

STEP 6 — JSON schema (house rule): web/_schemas/external/fx-rates-response.schema.json describing the expected response (amount number, base string const 'GBP', date string format date, rates object with patternProperties ^[A-Z]{3}$ → number exclusiveMinimum 0), every property described, $comment pointing at g2ml_fxValidateResponse() which enforces the same rules in code.

STEP 7 — tests. tests/unit/fx_rates_test.php: ValidateResponse (a good response; base 'EUR' → bad_base; a future date → bad_date; a date 10 days old with max 5 → stale; a negative rate, a string rate, a lowercase code or 61 entries → bad_rates; not an array → false); ShouldFetch (never → true; 3 hours ago → false; 21 hours ago → true); Approximate ('4.99' × '1.79' with 2 decimals → '8.93'; with 0 decimals → '9'); FetchRaw refuses an http:// address without calling the seam. tests/unit/cron_dispatch_test.php: 'exchange_rates' accepted. tests/integration/fx_rates_test.php (DB guards, fetch seam returning canned JSON): the job stores the rows and the status; a second run within 20 hours is skipped; a failing fetch keeps the old rows and writes an error status; g2ml_fxGetRate('CAD') returns the rate when fresh and null after rateDate is set 10 days back; the fx_enabled switch off → nothing fetched.

STEP 8 — docs (last): docs/DATABASE.md (the table and settings); docs/DEPLOYMENT.md (the job, the source, how to change it, and that nothing appears until the scheduled trigger runs); PRE_LAUNCH_CHECKLIST.md: '⏳ owner check — confirm Frankfurter''s current terms and the ECB reuse conditions are acceptable for showing approximate prices (decision 40)'; handoff.

VERIFY: php -l on every touched file; php tests/run.php, exit code read directly; integration with a database; import schema 047 and migration 047 twice; one real curl to the source address (state the result in the commit, or that the network was not available).
acceptance_criteria: tblExchangeRates (schema 047, migration 047) holds the latest GBP-based rate per currency with the source's date and the fetch time

The scheduled job 'exchange_rates' (also part of 'all') fetches at most once a day from a configurable https address with no secret, validates the response strictly, and stores all rates in one transaction

Any failure leaves the stored rates untouched and records an error status; g2ml_fxGetRate() returns nothing when a rate is missing or older than pricing.fx_max_age_days, so the approximate figure is simply not shown
The rate source (Frankfurter, ECB reference rates) and its terms are documented, with an owner check on the pre-launch checklist; the fetch never runs from a visitor's page load
Unit and integration tests with a fetch test seam; JSON schema for the response; suites green
PF-14.new_issue_title: 💱 [Pricing] Daily exchange rate for approximate prices on the pricing page
PF-14.new_issue_body:
## What and why

Owner decision 40 (#243, second set): the pricing page shows prices in GBP, plus fixed USD and EUR prices the owner sets. For any other currency it adds an 'approximately' figure, labelled as charged in GBP, from a daily exchange rate fetched by the scheduled job. The figure is for information only; the price charged never changes, and real prices are never converted automatically.

## Rate source

[Frankfurter](https://frankfurter.dev): free, open source, needs no account or key, and publishes the European Central Bank's reference rates once per working day. The ECB says these rates are for information only and allows reuse with the source acknowledged. The page names the source and the date next to any approximate figure. The address is a setting, so it can be changed without code.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] New table `tblExchangeRates` (schema 047, migration 047): the latest rate per currency, with the date the source gives and when we fetched it.
- [ ] A scheduled job `exchange_rates` (also run by `all`) that fetches at most once a day, checks the answer strictly, and stores it in one step.
- [ ] Fail safe: if a fetch fails, the old rates stay; if the stored rate is missing or older than a few days, the approximate figure is simply not shown.
- [ ] Never fetched during a visitor's page load.
- [ ] Status visible to GlobalAdmins; settings documented; the owner confirms the source's terms before launch.
- [ ] Unit and integration tests; a JSON schema for the response.

## Dependencies

The daily counts item (same cron file, built earlier), the prices admin (same overview page). The job only runs once the scheduled trigger is wired (#178); until then no approximate figures appear.

CX-02.title: Installer's collation fix runs a constant ALTER DATABASE, not one built from text (Codex catch-up finding)
CX-02.plan:
SOURCE: Codex's catch-up review (2026-09-25 09:42, the product-code commits on the working branch) found that SX-196's installer collation check (commit cc61e98) builds its correction as text: $db->query('ALTER DATABASE `' . $dbName . '` CHARACTER SET utf8mb4 COLLATE utf8mb4_unicode_ci'). The name is checked against /^[A-Za-z0-9_$-]{1,64}$/ first, so it is not exploitable, but the house rule is 'never string-built SQL'. Codex suggested preparing a constant, nameless statement. The lead tested that on 2026-09-25: MySQL 8.4.11 REFUSES ALTER DATABASE as a prepared statement (ERROR 1295 'This command is not supported in the prepared statement protocol yet'; collation unchanged), while MariaDB 11.8.9 accepts it. So a prepared statement would silently break the automatic correction on MySQL. Evidence: comment on #196.
STEP 1 - web/Go2My.Link/public_html/install/index.php, the collation check (around lines 370-450): (a) replace the string-built ALTER with the constant, nameless statement $db->query('ALTER DATABASE CHARACTER SET utf8mb4 COLLATE utf8mb4_unicode_ci'); it applies to the connection's selected database, and g2ml_install_connect() passes $creds['name'] as that database (check this before relying on it). (b) Delete the name-validation block (the preg_match on $dbName) and its error message, which exist only to make the name safe to paste into the SQL. (c) Keep the re-check after the ALTER and the existing message for when the correction fails (for example no ALTER privilege). (d) A SHORT comment, every statement checkable: nothing is pasted into this SQL, because the connection already selects the database; it is not a prepared statement because MySQL 8.4 refuses ALTER DATABASE in the prepared-statement protocol (error 1295, checked 2026-09-25; MariaDB accepts it); it contains no user input. (e) Remove any variable left unused. The remaining installer messages stay plain English, like the rest of the installer: whether the installer should be translatable is owner question #275, not part of this item.
STEP 2 - test: extend tests/unit/collation_docs_test.php or add a small static test that fails if install/index.php again builds an ALTER DATABASE statement by joining text (for example a match on ALTER DATABASE followed by a backtick-quote-dot, or any ALTER DATABASE string that is concatenated), and that passes on the constant statement. Keep it simple and explain the rule in one or two lines.
STEP 3 - docs: grep docs/, DEV_NOTES.md, PRE_LAUNCH_CHECKLIST.md and README.md for the removed message ('contains a character this installer will not place') or for text saying the installer validates the database name; update anything that is no longer true. Change nothing else.
VERIFY: php -l on the changed file; the TESTS; and a manual check in a throwaway container (docker run --rm, named after this item, for example cx02-mysql) that a PHP mysqli connection with the database selected, running the constant statement through query(), really changes a utf8mb4_general_ci database to utf8mb4_unicode_ci on mysql:8.4 (and on mariadb:11 if it is quick). Confirm afterwards that no container of that name remains and docker volume ls -q -f dangling=true is empty. Say in deviations_from_plan what was and was not checked.
acceptance_criteria: The installer's ALTER DATABASE statement is a constant string: no database name or other value is joined into it, and the name-validation block and its message are gone.
A short comment says why the statement is nameless and why it is not a prepared statement (MySQL 8.4 error 1295).
A unit test fails if a text-built ALTER DATABASE statement returns to the installer.
The automatic correction is shown to still work on MySQL 8.4 in a throwaway container (MariaDB too if quick), with the container and its data removed afterwards; tests pass.

extra_issues.title: 🕓 [Dashboard] Show times in each user's own time zone
extra_issues.body:
## What and why

Owner decision 43 (#243, second set): once PHP runs in UTC (#214), the dashboard shows times in UTC for now, with a follow-up to show each user's own time zone. This is that follow-up.

After #214, PHP and the database both work in UTC, which the security timers need. Nobody's own time zone was used for display before either. Each user's profile already stores a time zone (tblUsers, used by the LinksPage scheduled-links form), so the information exists. It just is not used when times are shown.

## Suggested approach

- One display helper, for example `g2ml_formatUserDateTime(string $utcDateTime, ?string $userTimezone, string $format): string`, that converts a stored UTC value to the user's zone for display only and falls back to UTC when the zone is missing or invalid. Stored values and comparisons stay in UTC.
- Show the zone next to times where it matters (for example '14:05 BST'), and in tables add a note saying which zone is used.
- Use it on every screen that shows a stored time: links, statistics (day boundaries need care: the per-day statistics are grouped by UTC day), API keys (expiry), sessions, LinksPage scheduled links, data-export pages, audit logs, and the security report inbox.
- The SX-214 commit body lists the display-only uses it found; start from that list.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A pure, unit-tested helper converts UTC to the user's zone for display, with a UTC fallback.
- [ ] Every dashboard screen that shows a stored time uses it; nothing written to the database changes.
- [ ] Statistics say clearly that days are UTC days, or are regrouped by the user's day (decide in the issue).
- [ ] Strings through `__()`; accessibility unchanged.

## Dependencies

#214 (PHP set to UTC).

extra_issues.title: 🧾 [Compliance] Write a JSON Schema for the whole data-export file
extra_issues.body:
## What and why

The house rule is that every JSON file the project writes has a schema beside it that describes every property. The subject-access data export (`g2ml_requestDataExport()` in `web/_functions/data_rights.php`) writes one JSON file per request, and it has no schema. Planning #245 (LP-34) found this: that item adds a schema only for the two new LinksPage sections it creates (`web/_schemas/export/linkspage-custom-code.schema.json`).

A full schema would document exactly what a person receives, make the export easier to check in a legal review, and let a test catch a section being dropped or renamed by accident.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `web/_schemas/export/data-export.schema.json` describes every top-level section and every property, with descriptions and required markers, referencing the LinksPage sections' schema.
- [ ] A test builds an export for a seeded test user and validates it against the schema by hand-written checks (there is no JSON Schema validator library, and Composer is not available).
- [ ] docs/DATABASE.md points at the schema.

## Dependencies

Best done after the LinksPage programme's export changes (LP-16, LP-31, LP-32, LP-34) have landed, so the schema describes the final shape.

extra_issues.title: 🔀 [Organisations] Offer to move an individual's existing links and LinksPages into an organisation when they create or join one
extra_issues.body:
## What and why

When someone who has been using Go2My.Link on their own creates or joins an organisation, their earlier short links and LinksPages stay attached to their individual account (they keep the shared `[default]` organisation). That is the existing behaviour, and owner decision 26 (#243) keeps it: their personal plan, if they have one, stays with them and applies again if they leave. It was noted as a follow-up during planning (LP-22).

Some people will want their earlier links and pages to belong to the new organisation, so the team can manage them and they count towards the team's plan. Others will not. The choice should be theirs.

## Suggested approach

- After creating or joining an organisation, offer a one-time choice: 'Move my existing links and LinksPages to <organisation>' or 'Keep them as mine'.
- Moving changes `orgHandle` on the person's own `[default]` links and pages in one transaction, checks the organisation's limits first (and explains what does not fit), and is logged.
- Consider what happens to API keys, custom domains and statistics attribution, and whether moving back on leaving is offered.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The person chooses; nothing moves without their consent.
- [ ] Limits are checked before anything moves; the move is all-or-nothing.
- [ ] Tests cover moving, refusing, and a move that would exceed the organisation's plan.

## Dependencies

The personal account holder (PF-13) and the page limit per organisation (#239).
